articleTitle: Multi-Role Consensus Through LLMs Discussions for Vulnerability Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Recent advancements in large language models (LLMs) have highlighted the potential for vulnerability de-tection, a crucial component of software quality assurance. Despite this progress, most studies have been limited to the perspective of a single role, usually testers, lacking diverse viewpoints from different roles in a typical software de-velopment life-cycle, including both developers and testers. To this end, this paper introduces a multi-role approach to employ LLMs to act as different roles simulating a real-life code review process and engaging in discussions toward a consensus on the existence and classification of vulnerabilities in the code. Preliminary evaluation of this approach indicates a 13.48% increase in the precision rate, an 18.25% increase in the recall rate, and a 16.13% increase in the F1 score.

articleTitle: Hardware Trojan Detection with Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: The small scale, high stealthiness, and significant destructive potential of Hardware Trojans (HTs) have attracted researchers' attention to detect them accurately. Existing research methods have certain limitations, such as the inability to detect unknown HTs, poor scalability, and incomplete feature representation. To overcome these limitations, we propose DFF, a feature fusion model based on graph neural networks. We represent the register transfer level (RTL) code as an abstract syntax tree (AST) and extract features from different perspectives using graph convolutional networks (GCN) and graph attention networks (GAT). Then, we perform feature fusion based on long short-term memory (LSTM) and utilize the fused features for HT detection. We validated our model on an extended dataset based on Trust-hub [1], and the experimental results demonstrate that our model achieves an average improvement of approximately 6.6% in terms of F1 score compared to other works.

articleTitle: C-Rusted: Safe and Secure Programming in Standard C
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: C-rusted is an innovative technology whereby C programs can be annotated so as to express ownership and borrowing of resources and several other non-trivial program properties, which can be formally verified through static analysis thus achieving strong safety and security guarantees.

articleTitle: Towards Simplification of Failure Scenarios for Machine Learning-Enabled Autonomous Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Scenario-based testing is an essential way of im-proving the safety and reliability of machine learning-enabled autonomous systems (MLAS), such as autonomous driving systems (ADS). As the complexity of failure scenarios in-creases with the development of more realistic MLAS testing approaches, it becomes essential to simplify failure scenarios to understand and identify the root causes of failures. In this vision paper, we present our vision to leverage search-based software engineering (SBSE) and surrogate-assisted optimisation (SAO) to address the challenges of simplifying failure scenarios in MLAS.

articleTitle: Reliability Evaluation of Classroom Teaching with MCI in College Based on the DFT Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Currently, multimedia computer-assisted instruction (MCI) has been widely used in colleges for classroom teaching, which can improve the teaching effect. Traditional teaching evaluation of the MCI mainly focuses on human factors. However, the MCI equipment's performance and device operation experience can also impact the teaching effect. Hence, the effect of teaching using MCI depends on the reliability of humans, machines, and human-machine interaction, which is not paid enough attention to. Addressing this point, this paper proposes a reliability model to evaluate college classroom teaching with the MCI based on the dynamic fault tree (DFT) since the DFT can describe dependency between basic events. The prime factors in classroom teaching with the MCI effect are extracted. The failure causal relationships between prime factors and the MCI equipment, teaching-learning, and human-machine interaction are analyzed, respectively. Based on the data we collected, the results show that the device's reliability directly impacts the whole reliability of the MCI teaching. The proposed method can display the reliability of the MCI teaching effect more realistically and provide decision-making support for teaching reform.

articleTitle: Review of Key Attribute Analysis and Verification Techniques for CPS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: In the key application fields of Cyber-Physical Systems, such as unmanned control systems, there are very strict requirements for system safety, real-time and other key attributes. However, the characteristics of CPS pose great challenges to their attribute analysis and verification. In this paper, the related works of key attribute verification of CPS is deeply analyzed, the classification of research methods is summarized, and the hot spots and difficulties in this field are pointed out.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Performance Resilience of Serverless Applications using Chaos Engineering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: This study explores the use of chaos engineering in evaluating the performance and resilience of serverless applications, which are built as complex distributed systems subject to different types of failures and errors. By intentionally injecting controlled failures and uncertainty into the system, we evaluate the impact of random delay injections on Lambda functions using two methods: one during code execution and the other during runtime. Our research aims to evaluate the performance and resilience of Lambda functions under controlled chaos experiments and study the impact of faults on serverless applications' behaviour by comparing the results with the baseline data regarding performance metrics.

articleTitle: SA-P2T: Sparse Attention-based Pyramid Pooling Transformer Network for Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Recently, Transformer has demonstrated superior performance in object detection tasks by virtue of its powerful capability of modeling image global information. However, due to Transformer's expensive computational overhead and high memory occupation, the detection efficiency and performance are often affected when processing high-resolution or long sequence images. Later, some improvement works reduced the size of key and value in Transformer through pooling or convolution operations, which alleviated the above problems to a certain extent. Nonetheless, due to the smooth-ness of image data itself, the image patches in the smooth region do not contribute significantly to the final output of the model, resulting in data redundancy. Therefore, we propose a novel Sparse Attention-based Pyramid Pooling Transformer Network (SA-P2T) for object detection. Specifically, in SA-P2T, we introduce a sparse attention module, which measures the query sparsity via the Kullback-Leibler divergence, and then screen out the query that makes a large contribution to the self-attention as the new query. This module can filter out redundant information while retaining essential information, enabling the model to process image data more efficiently, and further reducing the computational complexity and memory space occupation of the model. Our experimental results on MS-COCO dataset illustrate that SA-P2T not only reduces computational complexity, but also enhances the accuracy and speed of detection, demonstrating the effectiveness of our proposed method. The code will be released at https://github.com/Genbao-Xu/SA-P2T.

articleTitle: Failure Modelling and Analysis of Airborne Video Transmission System Based on Data Reliability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: The correctness of business data carried by airborne video transmission system is crucial to the construction of advanced situational awareness capability, it is necessary to identify, analyse and optimise the weak links in the system that may lead to data errors, and to improve the data reliability. To address this problem, a video data fault modelling and diagnosis method is proposed based on the Bayesian model. By sorting out the video transmission architecture and requirements, an airborne video data error fault tree is constructed, the fault tree is transformed based on the Bayesian model, fault training subsets are obtained by preclassifying the original faults, and the system reliability and weak links are analysed using the Bayesian network model. The simulation results show that compared with the existing reliability analysis methods, the proposed method can achieve effective evaluation and predictive repair of system data reliability.

articleTitle: Research on Intelligent Recognition and Analysis of Power Grid Infrastructure Construction Based on YOLO
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Power grid construction sites pose challenges like clutter, occlusion, and varying scales, making manual monitoring insufficient. Employing image recognition technology is crucial to track personnel, safety compliance, and vehicle entry in real time. Despite limited data availability, our study achieves 90% accuracy using transfer learning with a small dataset. This adaptable model not only identifies elements in power grid sites but also accommodates diverse task demands.

articleTitle: Pedestrian Detection Method Based on Fusion of LIDAR and Camera
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: As two important sensors in the perception process of autonomous driving, LIDAR is weak in judging target details, and camera typically have more demanding requirements regarding light conditions. In order to overcome the limitations of single sensor in pedestrian detection, a pedestrian detection method based on the fusion of laser radar and camera is proposed. Firstly, the M1 solid-state LIDAR is temporally and spatially synchronised with the camera, and then the point cloud is processed to achieve point cloud downsampling and ground point cloud removal and the processed point cloud is clustered using the density-based DBSCAN clustering algorithm. Concurrently, the camera image is used to detect pedestrians using the YOLOv5 visual target detection algorithm. Finally, the detection results of the two sensors are fused by decision level fusion to obtain the final detection information. The experiments carried out in the campus scene confirm that the accuracy of the proposed method for pedestrian fusion detection is 85.7%, and it solves the problem of missed detection of visual detection caused by light factors of camera sensors.

articleTitle: Capacity and Time Reliability Evaluation for Time-Varying Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Facing the challenges caused by Time-Varying Networks (TVNs), this paper proposes a capacity and time reliability evaluation method. The Time Aggregated Graph (TAG) and line graph are combined for modeling TVNs. Additionally, modeling steps of the existing line graph model is simplified to accelerate its generation. Then, the capacity and time reliability evaluation method is proposed through finding the minimal path sets considering both capacity demand and time requirements associated with timestamps (TS-d-t-MPs) of the TVN in multiple Monte Carlo iterations. A park road network is used as a case to demonstrate its solution procedure in evaluating the capacity and time reliability of TVN s.

articleTitle: The Colour Temperature Intensity Adjusting Model for Improving Naked Eye 3D Holographic Computer Projection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: The aim of this study is to improve the algorithm design flaws of high-density 3D colour projection published in 2023 Optica computer journal [1]. The result of this study is the colour temperature-based intensity model. The purpose of getting the model is for adjusting the proportion usage between the conventional multi-plane projection algorithm and high-density multi-plane projection algorithm. Additionally, the study is to enrich CIEXYZ Colour space in the perspective of human-computer interaction by colour intensity perception. The unique finding of the result shows, it's important to set the filter to separate the cool zone and the warm zone when modelling the colour intensity model for improving naked eye 3D holographic computer projection.

articleTitle: How to Choose a Suitable Method in Image Semantic Segmentation-An Experimental Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Image semantic segmentation is a fundamental task in image processing and has been applied in urban planning, smart agriculture and many other research areas. High precision semantic segmentation results are an important foundation for image analysis and application. Although many methods have been proposed in image semantic segmentation, a comprehensive analysis of the effectiveness of these methods is lacking. Therefore, in this paper, six commonly used image semantic segmentation methods, namely DenseNet, EfficientNet, Inception, ResNet, InceptionResNet and VGG16, their main advantages and disadvantages are analyzed and discussed. And then, the effectiveness of these methods were verified through an experimental study.

articleTitle: Software fault localization based on eigenvector centrality in complex network theory
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Software debugging plays a crucial role in fault localization tasks, and spectrum-based fault localization (SBFL) is a hot topic in software automation debugging research. However, existing SBFL technologies are generally limited by tie within ranks, where a large number of elements share the same suspiciousness, which in turn severely limits the performance of SBFL. To this end, we propose an SBFL model based on eigenvector centrality (FLEC). This algorithm first utilizes the statement coverage information in the program spectrum to construct a statement network, and adopts the correlation between statements as edge weights. Then, FLEC takes statement suspiciousness as node weight. On this basis, the algorithm utilizes the eigenvector centrality to calculate the weighted suspiciousness of each statement while considering both node importance and correlation between nodes. Finally, FLEC conducted experimental validation on 3 datasets of Defects4J, and the results showed an average improvement of 10.7% in ACC@N compared to the optimal baseline.

articleTitle: Aircraft Pose Perception Technology Based on Tire Detection for Automatic Docking of Towbarless Aircraft Tractors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Aircraft tractors are crucial airport ground support equipment that play an indispensable role in assisting aircraft during transfers. The prevalent towbarless aircraft tractor currently requires manual operation for the tractor to engage with the aircraft tires through its clamping lifting system, a process often deemed inefficient. This study explores a LiDAR-based technology for detecting aircraft position and attitude during tractor docking. Initially, a Generalized-Iterative Closest Point (GICP) method is employed to create a point cloud model of the aircraft tires. Subsequently, the identified scene is matched with the tire model to calculate the position and attitude of the aircraft tire in the scene, achieving an error performance of only 4.8%. In addition, the study utilized geometric information from the front and rear landing gears of the aircraft to predict the position of the rear wheels when the front wheels were obscuring the rear wheels, which was ignored in previous studies. This system, devoid of complex hardware requirements, solely necessitates the pre-collection of aircraft tire information and can be seamlessly integrated into various towbarless aircraft tractors. It caters to the efficiency demands of contemporary tractors in the aircraft docking process. The main contribution of this study is the application of point cloud recognition technology to aircraft attitude recognition, which lays the foundation for automatic docking of aircraft tractors in the future.

articleTitle: Large Language Models on Solving Integral Calculus Problems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: This article evaluates the ability of language mo-dels (LLMs), such as GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 Turbo, to support learning, especially in solving mathematical problems. A com-parative experiment was carried out, including models with and without fine-tuning, where GPT-4 obtained the best performance, solving 94% of the questions. The results indicate challenges in algebraic expressions and fractions, highlighting the importance of personalized training for specific tasks.

articleTitle: Public Perception Toward Tesla Fatal Accidents: Neural Network Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: This study endeavors to comprehensively evaluate the impact that fatal accidents involving autonomous vehicles, with a focus on incidents associated with Tesla, have on the public's perception of this technology. To achieve this, we systematically collect and examine user interactions on Twitter, encompassing the period both before and after such accidents occur. By employing a sophisticated Siamese neural network model for our analysis, we are able to effectively identify and quantify shifts in public sentiment and discourse regarding autonomous vehicles. The results of our investigation reveal a nuanced landscape of public opinion, characterized by a significant alteration in perception following these incidents. Specifically, our findings delineate a complex dynamic where, alongside an increased acceptance of autonomous vehicle technology, there exists a persistent and substantial concern regarding its safety and reliability. This study not only sheds light on the immediate reaction of the public to fatal accidents involving autonomous vehicles but also contributes to a deeper understanding of the broader societal implications of adopting such technology. Through this analysis, we underscore the importance of addressing public safety concerns and enhancing communication strategies to foster a more informed and balanced discourse around the future of autonomous vehicle technology.

articleTitle: Survey on the Impact of Agile Development on Software Quality
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Software quality has grown increasingly significant in the information society nowadays. As information technology advances, software has permeated all aspects of social life. Our survey investigates the quality of domestic software products, encompassing the overall state of software quality, requirement quality, design quality, code quality, test quality, the focus of team efforts for the upcoming year, and the application and user experience of large models. Moreover, we analyze the impact of the prevalent agile development methodology on various aspects of software quality.

articleTitle: PreBEV: Leveraging Predictive Flow for Enhanced Bird's-Eye View 3D Dynamic Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Recently, the 3D object detection problem in the autonomous driving vehicle based on the look-around camera has introduced the spatio-temporal consistency to improve the detection or instance prediction performance. Dense BEV spatial features and rich temporal information are expected to make up for the lack of object attention, ignoring the importance of dynamic target motion and position information in future image frames. We propose a novel framework called PreBEV. PreBEV introduces the predictive stream method to construct the query anchor box and learns the implicit motion characteristics of sequence images through the close association with pixels, which effectively utilizes the adaptability of BEV and image views to alleviate the computational pressure caused by dense queries. In addition, this framework proposes BEV feature fusion based on predictive flow guidance, which avoids the limitations of traditional simple time-series fusion strategies (weighted sum, series) set by hand, makes full use of the motion characteristics of objects and improves the attention to dynamic objects. PreBEV effectively simplifies the multi-task objective and improves the prediction stability and detection accuracy. The experimental results show that PreBEV performs superior on the NuScenes dataset, which brings a new research paradigm to the field of BEV detection.

articleTitle: Research on Intelligent Relic Interpretation System Based on a Large Language Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Nowadays, docents are the main force for inheriting and displaying human cultural heritage. However, the experience of visitors largely depends on their knowledge depth and updates. Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated promising results across various fields due to their robust linguistic intelligence acquired through extensive data training. Nevertheless, training LLMs remains challenging due to their high hardware requirements. How can we integrate a LLM into a relic interpretation system without the need for extensive training? To this end, a solution is proposed by combining a LLM with a private domain database to create an intelligent relic interpretation system. This system encompasses the following functionalities:(1) Speech recognition and synthesis: Users input speech, and the system utilizes speech recognition technology to convert the speech into text. This text is then processed by the LLM, and the model's responses are synthesized into speech output; (2) Professional knowledge explanation: Leveraging a LLM and a private domain database to achieve more accurate and professional responses, compared to simply fine-tuning LLMs, this allows for the application of LLMs in vertical fields without the need for additional training; (3) Private domain database renewal: Two methods for updating the database are used: extracting relevant data from intranet sources and uploading data by professionals. The performance of the system is evaluated through comparison and ablation experiments. The results demonstrate that the system effectively addresses the limitations of traditional relic interpretation methods and introduces novel perspectives for relic interpretation.

articleTitle: The Most Important Factors Chosen in Medical Clinical Data by Using Multi-Facet Clustering Variational Autoencoders (MFCVAE)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: In medical practice, doctors often need the support of various medical measuring data to diagnose diseases. In clinical observation, doctors will sort out various factors related to the cause of the disease based on the patient's condition. MFCVAE is a principled, probabilistic clustering model which finds multiple partitions of data simultaneously through its multiple Mixtures-of-Gaussians (MoG) prior. Our model lies in the framework of variational autoencoders, and is trained fully unsupervised. MFCVAE discovers a disentangled multi-facet structure in an exploratory setting, allows to compose representations of inputs in the latent space, perform generative classification, and generate diverse, synthetic samples. This article used the patient data of hospital patients and the MFCVAE method be used to find the most relevant factors and provide them as a reference for doctors in disease diagnosis. The research results was shown that the top 10 important factors could be found from 186 clinical factors using the MFCVAE method.

articleTitle: Research on the Integration Method of Software Static Testing Tools Based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: The reliability of autonomous control software is critical to the power grid's operational safety, necessitating reliable means to assure software quality. Static analysis, with its ability to function autonomously, be deployed earlier, and operate without executing code, has been extensively adopted for testing software, becoming a vital tool in ensuring the quality of power grid dispatch automatic control software. Given the plethora of static analysis tools available, each with their unique strengths and varying levels of sensitivity and specificity, addressing their significant rates of false positives and negatives has emerged as a crucial challenge. This study leverages the data from defect detection reports of CppCheck, TscanCode, and Flawfinder, three leading open-source static analysis tools, along with GaussianNB, RF, and KNN — three machine learning classification algorithms. By integrating the analysis from these tools, defects are accurately segregated into true and false positives, with the latter being strategically filtered out. It achieves a substantial increase in the precision of the integrated defect report based on a small reduction in the overall recall rate, providing guidance and reference for the static analysis of grid dispatch automatic control software.

articleTitle: Hybrid Attention Based Spatiotemporal Neural Network in Lifetime Prognostics of Lithium Batteries
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: As an important part of new energy vehicles and electronic devices fields, predicting the state of health (SOH) of lithium batteries is crucial for improving the safety of battery use, extending battery life and optimizing the battery management system. Traditionally, features are extracted from various signals of the battery to build a mathematical or data-driven model of the lithium battery. The key issue is how to use existing features of Li-ion batteries to capture Li-ion battery degradation trends. One feasible option is to select features based on their correlation with SOH. This paper aims to investigate the relationship between different features using multi-dimensional time series features and high-dimensional spatial features. Both temporal and spatial features are fused by a polynomial module. In order to improve the accuracy of SOH estimation, a hybrid parallel multi-head attention network module is selected for these features. The performance of the proposed method is validated on two independent publicly available datasets, and the experiments show that the proposed method achieves the lowest mean absolute error (MAE) and the lowest root mean square error (RMSE).

articleTitle: Granger Causality Analysis Between Sensor Data Based on Deep Gaussian Process Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: The growing ubiquity of sensors in complex industrial systems has led to the incorporation of extensive sensor networks for system health monitoring. However, a crucial aspect often overlooked is the presence of interdependencies within the sensor data itself. This lack of consideration hinders a thorough comprehension of the system's dynamic behavior. This paper proposes a novel approach that leverages Granger causality and deep Gaussian process regression to unveil the influence between monitored sensor values to gain deeper insights into system behavior. We test our approach based on data generated by an underlying Glass-Mackey model. The results demonstrate the approach can effectively identify interdependence and causality. This research contributes to a more comprehensive understanding of sensor interdependencies, offering a fresh perspective on sensor configuration and system health state analysis.

articleTitle: Research on the Impact of Tester's Technical and Cognitive Factors on Aerospace Software Test Quality
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: This paper primarily analyzes the impact of tester capabilities on the quality of aerospace software testing and elaborates on how to assess tester abilities from both technical and cognitive perspectives. The research was supported by the Aerospace Software Testing Center of the China Aerospace Science and Industry Corporation (CASIC), which allowed researchers to collect data on the center's testing personnel and conduct interviews with relevant testers. The findings of this research have been used by the center to coordinate the efforts to improve quality and human resource management. This paper provides valuable insights and guidance for the field of aerospace software testing, contributing to the enhancement of tester capabilities and software testing quality, and ultimately promoting the reliability and safety of aerospace software.

articleTitle: Harmonization of Security Standards for Embedded Systems in a Comprehensive Metamodel: The Security Abstraction Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: The development of reliable systems is inextricably linked to the consideration of security aspects during the development process. Especially in the context of autonomous vehicles, security is crucial to ensure user trust in this technology. This work presents an overview of the harmonization of the Security Abstration Model (SAM). The results demonstrate that our approach is compliant with relevant security standards for embedded systems, indicating compliance and robustness. The utilization of SAM improves conceptual understanding and promotes clarity in security engineering.

articleTitle: Histogram Publication with Shuffled Differential Privacy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a histogram publication algorithm HP-SDP (histogram publication with shuffled differential privacy) for the existing histogram publication methods, which is difficult to effectively balance the user privacy and the collector's analyzing accuracy at the same time. The algorithm combines the shuffled response mechanism SRR (shuffled randomized response) designed by the local data encryption technique, which can perturb the user data in a linear decomposition manner, and a uniform random arrangement algorithm MRS (message random shuffling) based on heap arrangement technique, which is able to shuffle all the user's data using the MRS. Using MRS to randomly arrange all users' messages, the shuffled messages satisfy the centralized differential privacy, which makes the malicious collector unable to screen the identity of the target user through the link between the message and the user. The experimental results of the HP-SDP algorithm and the existing histogram publishing algorithms on two kinds of datasets show that the publishing accuracy is better than the similar algorithms.

articleTitle: A Data Constraint Analysis Method for Full-Digital Simulation Test
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: At present, software testing is an effective approach to ensure and improve software quality. However, there is a lack of data dependency analysis methods for constructing full-digital test data scripts, which results in the problem that constructed test data scripts maybe hard to simulate the real-world mission scenarios of the weapon embedded software. To solve this problem, this paper clarifies the emphasis of data constraint analysis is sporadic data by analyzing the external data features of the weapon embedded software, and then proposes a data constraint analysis method based on profile and directed graph. The proposed method can complete the analysis of data constraints from coarse-grained to fine-grained efficiently. Moreover, according to the analysis results, full-digital testing test data script that can simulate the real-world mission scenarios of the software can be constructed. Experiment results have proven that the proposed method is effective and can improve analysis efficiency.

articleTitle: A Graph-Based Approach for Discovering Evidence Relationships Across Multiple Devices in Group Crimes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: This study presents a new approach for identifying connections among evidence scattered across various devices. By employing a relational Digital Forensic Knowledge Graph (rDFKG), which integrates several Digital Forensic Knowl-edge Graphs (DFKGs) and a set of predetermined relationships between them, this method automatically reveals insights into crimes committed by groups.

articleTitle: Generating Adversarial Samples Based on the Attack Robust Training Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: In this paper, we study the problem of black-box attack and propose a new adversarial sample generation framework to attack the robust trained model (ARTM). Iterative methods can cause serious overfitting problems because they only consider the optimality of a single adversarial sample and ignore the entire sample distribution. The generative approach maps the entire original sample distribution to the target model attack space. However, such methods are also limited by the similarity of the decision boundary between the substitute model and the target model, and the difference of the boundary will affect the adversarial sample transferability. Hence, we aim to mitigate this impact by adjusting the decision boundaries of the substitute model. Through robustness training, the model decision boundary is smoother, and the distribution of adversarial samples will reduce some noise and become more concentrated. This also makes the substitute model boundary more similar to the target model, thus improving the transferability of adversarial sample. Our proposed framework offers a fresh perspective for adversarial sample generation and robust training. The experimental results based on the ImageNet dataset show that our method is effective.

articleTitle: Vulnerability Prediction and Assessment Using Software Product Metrics and Machine Learning: What Does Not Work
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Software metrics can help developers improve their written code by providing an overview of already written code. In the long term, they can thus help increase the software's quality. There are a variety of metrics and tools that calculate them. This study aims to determine whether they can also be used to make statements about software security, particularly to predict the number of vulnerabilities present. We use the CVEfixes dataset, a recent version of the CVE database, extract the corresponding code with and without vulnerabilities and calculate the software metrics using Understand and Analizo tools. Based on these metrics, we try to predict the presence of a vulnerability or its severity using a neural network. Unfortunately, the network was not able to make any meaningful predictions from the metrics, so we are looking for causes of what can be improved in this context. We want to highlight issues that arise when calculating software metrics in open-source software.

articleTitle: Towards LLM-Enhanced Digital Twins of Intelligent Computing Center
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Digital twin techniques enable the digital modeling of the power and environmental systems of intelligent computing systems. However, the traditional analysis methods of digital twins do not integrated expert experience with data-driven approaches flexibly. They also analyze the information from multiple dimensions in isolation without considering their relations. This paper proposes a large language model-enhanced digital twin system for addressing these issues. The proposed system provides natural language-based interactive analysis, allowing experts to collaborate with algorithms for risk analysis; it employs a large language model-driven multi-agent system to simulate the interactions of the dynamic environmental systems, achieving multi-dimensional joint prediction. Additionally, this paper presents a case study to demonstrate the usefulness and effectiveness of the proposed system.

articleTitle: High Intensity Radar Echo Extrapolation Based on Stacked Generative Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: In recent years, the phenomenon of severe convective disaster weather has increased significantly in the world. Due to the characteristics of small spatial scale, short occurrence period, great destructiveness and drastic changes, severe convective disaster weather shows a high degree of randomness and uncertainty in its generation and extinction process. Machine learning is advancing rapidly, and made great strides in weather radar echoes extrapolation, but the existing radar echo extrapolation methods are mainly based on the finite observation dynamics of the flawed echo motion extrapolation paradigm, disregarding the echo sequence itself has a more intricate evolutionary process. High intensity echo region is easy to lose details in the convolution process, and the generated image is often fuzzy and distorted, resulting in low prediction accuracy. Consequently, we believe that the task of radar echo extrapolation is one of spatiotemporal series prediction. Based on the GAN model, which can generate high-resolution graphics, we propose a GL-GAN model structure, which is made up of the generator and discriminator, two competitive learning systems. Its generator is GL-PredNet, which is based on stack generation structure, and its discriminator is made up of one fully linked layer, one pooling layer, and five convolution layers. The loss function is optimized and the gradient difference error GDE is proposed. This improves the model's capacity to record and process high-intensity radar echoes' information, the fuzzy distortion of radar echoes is improved, and the model's performance in future frame prediction is improved. The findings demonstrate that, on average, the suggested model outperforms current deep learning models.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis of Comment Texts Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: With the rapid development of mobile Internet and the rapid popularization of social networks, a large number of netizens have commented on the Internet. How to mine valuable information from comment texts has become a research hotspot. This paper uses a bidirectional long short-term memory network model to process comment text data, obtaining contextual features from the front and back of the text sequence, which can better capture the positional information of sentences. On this basis, attention mechanism is used to capture the internal feature correlation of comment text sequence, effectively enhancing the model's ability to capture emotional information of comment text, and further improving the accuracy of sentiment tendency classification. The experimental results show that this model has achieved certain advantages in evaluation indicators such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 value.

articleTitle: Research on Simulation System Software Reliability Demonstration Testing Scheme Based on Nonparametric Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: In the process of acceptance software products, demonstration testing result is obtained based on the data in the reliability growth testing process, which leads to inability to truly reflect the reliability level of software. Therefore, this paper first proposes a software reliability demonstration testing scheme based on nonparametric method, and this scheme gives demonstration result without excessive increasing testing workload. Secondly, confidence analysis is performed to determine the true value range of failure probability. Finally, through a certain type of simulation system as an example, the feasibility of scheme is proved.

articleTitle: Why Students Write Low-Quality Unit Testing Scripts: An Empirical Study from Software Testing Skill Competitions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: We conducted an empirical study on 440 JUnit unit testing scripts collected from the Software Testing Skill Competitions. Findings reveal that: 1) The polarization of unit testing skills is severe. 2) The scores of the testing missions that provide the program flowchart are higher than others. In comparison, the scores of the testing missions that only provide textual descriptions of the program under are lower. 3) Test oracles are sometimes not taken seriously, resulting in the incorrect expected output. 4) Students usually perform better on testing missions of statement coverage and branch coverage but worse on the testing mission of condition coverage. The above findings may provide helpful suggestions for teachers in the education of unit testing.

articleTitle: Towards Safe Human-Robot Interaction: A Pilot Study on a Deep Learning-Assisted Workspace Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: This pilot study aims to explore the potential of a deep learning-assisted workspace monitoring system in ensuring safety in both social and industrial human-robot interaction settings. For this purpose, two vision sensors are used to collect multi-view datasets from different perspectives, with a single participant involved in 12 defined movement scenarios. The Residual Network (ResNet 18), a deep learning model, is employed to detect upper body movements based on the collected datasets. The experimental results demonstrate the accurate prediction of upper body movements by the proposed approach. Furthermore, the results also indicate the potential integration of this approach, which utilizes multiple inputs from various sensors, with the existing system introduced in previous work to facilitate a more dynamic workspace monitoring system for safety purposes.

articleTitle: The Economics of Blockchain Governance: Evaluate Liquid Democracy on the Internet Computer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Decentralized Autonomous Organizations (DAOs), utilizing blockchain technology to enable collective governance, are a promising innovation. This research addresses the ongoing query in blockchain governance: How can DAOs optimize human cooperation? Focusing on the Network Nervous System (NNS), a comprehensive on-chain governance framework underpinned by the Internet Computer Protocol (ICP) and liquid democracy principles, we employ theoretical abstraction and simulations to evaluate its potential impact on cooperation and economic growth within DAOs. Our findings emphasize the significance of the NNS's staking mechanism, particularly the reward multiplier, in aligning individual short-term interests with the DAO's long-term prosperity. This study contributes to the understanding and effective design of blockchain-based governance systems.

articleTitle: Solar Panel Fault Detection: Applying Convolutional Neural Network for Advanced Fault Detection in Solar-Hydrogen System at University
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: This study uses the Samcheok Campus of Kangwon National University as a case study inside a solar-hydrogen system to provide a novel method of advanced defect detection in solar panels. Although they are essential to renewable energy sources, solar panels can malfunction for a number of reasons. The inaccuracy and inefficiency of traditional defect detection approaches have led to the investigation of more advanced methods, such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). The study entails compiling and preprocessing an extensive dataset that covers a range of solar panel fault scenarios. Using this dataset, a CNN architecture is painstakingly created and trained, utilizing methods like data augmentation and normalization to increase model resilience. Partitioning the data into training and validation sets, putting optimization tactics into practice to reduce loss, and assessing the model using metrics like data accuracy and loss, training and validation Loss, and training and validation accuracy. are all part of the training process. Specific implementation elements are covered, such as software configuration, system requirements, and difficulties experienced during training. The results demonstrate how well and consistently the CNN model can identify different kinds of solar panel faults. Faults that have been identified are examined closely, and their implications for the operation of the solar-hydrogen system are discussed. The report also discusses its shortcomings and makes recommendations for further research directions. This research, which uses the Samcheok Campus of Kangwon National University as a case study, advances fault detection algorithms for solar panels and provides insights into the campus's solar-hydrogen system, which may improve its efficiency and dependability.

articleTitle: Formalization of Operational Domain and Operational Design Domain for Automated Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Specifying an Operational Design Domain (ODD) is crucial for safeguarding automated vehicle systems against conditions that exceed their capabilities. Yet, prior definitions of ODD have relied on ambiguous and unclear terms, resulting in numerous misunderstandings and misconceptions. This paper introduces a formal approach to clearly define the Operational Domain (OD) and ODD for automated vehicles. Furthermore, the absence of essential terms, such as the OD, has resulted in the creation of numerous terms that have made things more complicated and confusing. This level of complexity is unacceptable when it comes to developing safety-critical systems, where any uncertainty can lead to significant risks. This study addresses these deficiencies by providing a precise mathematical model of OD and clarifying its relationship with other terms. Also, by formalizing these terms, this work establishes a foundation for developing further concepts such as ODD specification and ODD monitoring, which are explained in this paper.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Green Campus: Solar Panel Fault Detection Using ResNet-50 for Solar-Hydrogen System in Universities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: The solar-hydrogen system installed at the Samcheok Campus of Kangwon National University is the setting for this paper's presentation of an AI-driven method for fault detection in solar panels. Ensuring the best performance and reliability of renewable energy systems is becoming increasingly important in educational institutions, such as universities. We suggest using the deep learning architecture ResNet-50 to automatically identify solar panel defects. We improved the ResNet-50 model for fault classification by preprocessing the dataset obtained from the campus's solar-hydrogen system. We evaluate the proposed method using metrics such as data accuracy and loss, training and validation loss, and training and validation accuracy, and we compare its performance with state-of-the-art defect identification systems. The experimental findings highlight the AI-driven defect detection system's effectiveness and its potential for in-the-moment solar panel installation monitoring and maintenance. We demonstrate the usefulness and advantages of integrating AI technology into green campuses using the case study of Kangwon National University Samcheok Campus. This work establishes the foundation for future research in AI -driven fault detection systems for renewable energy systems and advances sustainable energy management practices in educational institutions.

articleTitle: Vulnerability Classification on Source Code Using Text Mining and Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Nowadays, security testing is an integral part of the testing activities during the software development life-cycle. Over the years, various techniques have been proposed to identify security issues in the source code, especially vulnerabilities, which can be exploited and cause severe damages. Recently, Machine Learning (ML) techniques capable of predicting vulnerable software components and indicating high-risk areas have appeared, among others, accelerating the effort demanding and time consuming process of vulnerability localization. For effective subsequent vulnerability elimination, there is a need for automating the process of labeling detected vulnerabilities in vulnerability categories i.e., identifying the type of the vulnerability. Several techniques have been proposed over the years for automating the labeling process of vulnerabilities. However, the vast majority of the proposed methods attempt to identify the type of vulnerabilities based on their textual description that is provided by experts, such as the description provided by the vulnerability report in the National Vulnerability Database, and not on their actual source code, hindering their full automation and the vulnerability categorization from the software testing phase. This work examines the vulnerability classification directly from the source code during the vulnerability detection step. Moreover, this way, a vulnerability detection method will be able to provide complete information and interpretation of its findings. Leveraging the advances in the field of Artificial Intelligence and Natural Language Processing, we construct and compare several multi-class classification models for categorizing vulnerable code snippets. The results highlight the importance of the context-aware embeddings of the pre-trained Transformer-based models, as well as the significance of transfer learning from a programming language-related domain.

articleTitle: Decoding Social Sentiment in DAO: A Comparative Analysis of Blockchain Governance Communities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Blockchain technology is leading a revolutionary transformation across diverse industries, with effective governance as a critical determinant for the success and sustainability of blockchain projects. Community forums, pivotal in engaging decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs), wield a substantial impact on blockchain governance decisions. Concurrently, Natural Language Processing (NLP), particularly sentiment analysis, provides powerful insights from textual data. While prior research has explored the potential of NLP tools in social media sentiment analysis, a gap persists in understanding the sentiment landscape of blockchain governance communities. The evolving discourse and sentiment dynamics on the forums of top DAOs remain largely unknown. This paper delves deep into the evolving discourse and sentiment dynamics on the public forums of leading DeFi projects—Aave, Uniswap, Curve Dao, Yearn.finance, Merit Circle, and Balancer—placing a primary focus on discussions related to governance issues. Our study shows that participants in decentralized communities generally express positive sentiments during Discord discussions. Furthermore, there is a potential interaction between discussion intensity and sentiment dynamics, i.e., a higher discussion volume may contribute to a more stable sentiment from code analysis. The insights gained from this study are valuable for decision-makers in blockchain governance, underscoring the pivotal role of sentiment analysis in interpreting community emotions and its evolving impact on the landscape of blockchain governance. This research significantly contributes to the interdisciplinary exploration of the intersection of blockchain and society, specifically emphasizing the decentralized blockchain governance ecosystem. We provide our data and code for replicability as open access on GitHub11https://github.com/SciEcon/BlockchainSentiment2023.

articleTitle: MRM-LOOP:A Dynamic Visual Loop Closure Detection Algorithm Based on Motion Region Matching
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of false negatives and false positives in loop closure detection for visual SLAM algorithms in dynamic environments, a dynamic visual SLAM loop closure detection algorithm based on motion region matching named MRM-LOOP is proposed. Firstly, the VLAD local feature descriptor algorithm is used to extract the feature vectors of image feature points to ensure the stable correspondence between different images; Secondly, it uses the inter-frame motion vectors extracted from IMU data to enhance the robustness of feature matching and avoid false positive detection caused by camera pose mismatching; Finally, a region-weighted matching strategy is introduced to achieve more accurate loop closure detection by comparing the vector matching degree between the current frame and the historical frame and calculating the matching weight. The experimental results show that the proposed method can significantly improve the recall rate of loop detection in the open data set while maintaining the same accuracy, and the true positive detection probability is increased by 27.29% compared with the DBOW bag method when facing camera rotation. Correct loop detection can be realized in real dynamic environment data set. This paper provides a new solution for visual SLAM technology in dynamic environment.

articleTitle: Fine-tuning BERT for Intelligent Software System Fault Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: As software systems increasingly evolve towards intelligence, a multitude of new failure modes continue to emerge. Faced with a rapidly accumulating amount of complex software failures from multiple sources, quickly determining their categories of faults is a crucial step in enhancing the efficiency of fault resolution, optimizing resource allocation, and continuously improving software quality. The semantic understanding afforded by neural network language models paves the way for swift, automated categorization. However, the direct application of NLP models to software fault classification tends to require supplementary data from the development process and suffers from limited classifier generalization. To address the challenge of generating universal representations for software fault diagnosis, we introduce a novel classification framework leveraging a pre-trained BERT model for nuanced global feature extraction. This model harnesses deep learning techniques, including feedforward and transformer encoder layers, to capture and utilize the rich semantic nuances and domain-specific knowledge crucial for fault categorization. Validation on an independent dataset demonstrates that our BERT-Transformer outperforms competing models, achieving the highest precision and F1 score at 80% and 78.7%, show-casing its superior accuracy and robust generalization in fault classification tasks.

articleTitle: A Visualization Method for Association Analysis and Fusion Based on Large-Scale Polymorphic Information
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Based on mining the association relationship in the War Game data, this study extracts the key actions to provide support for the auxiliary operation deduction, operation process description and review evaluation. Based on the construction of evaluation system, relationship mining and target value ranking, this paper proposes a technical route to realize the analysis and fusion display method of operational relationship and action impact in war game data. According to the needs of different levels and angles, the distribution display and trend of data situation are presented on the visual interface. It provides theoretical guidance and practical reference for the design of deduction data fusion presentation, which is helpful to reduce the cognitive load of decision-makers, enhance situation awareness and improve decision-making efficiency.

articleTitle: Computational Imagination in Three-Dimension Scene Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Integrating emotional and behavioural data into 3D scene synthesis is an emerging area blending cognitive science with computational creativity to create more engaging, realistic, and emotionally resonant virtual environments. This study presents an interdisciplinary framework for generating 3D scenes from textual narratives, where emotional and physical metaphors guide the rendering process. The system utilises natural language processing techniques to identify behavioural patterns and emotional values in user-supplied sentences. These emotions determine the absolute position of the subject in the spatial matrix, placing those subjects with stronger emotional content closer to the observer. At the same time, the relative positions of subjects, predicates and objects utilise the metaphor of gravity to simulate an attraction-rejection dynamic similar to that of physical bodies in space. This ingenious positioning system is based on the laws of physics and allows for the construction of more situational 3D environments. The proposed model demonstrates how computational imagination can leverage physical principles to significantly enhance creativity in visual narrative and interaction design.

articleTitle: Deciphering Livestream Contents: OCR-Driven Thumbnail Forensic Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: The demand for digital forensics is continually increasing in the age of AI, the Internet of Things, and social media. The increase in the usage of live streaming platforms necessitates the development of techniques to analyze Livestream content. This research introduces an approach to forensic analysis employing Optical Character Recognition (OCR) technologies. Our methodology involves the application of advanced computer vision tools and image processing techniques to extract valuable contextual information from Thumbnails. This approach is particularly relevant in cases where the original Livestream data may have been deleted or unavailable. This research aims to contribute to advancing forensic methodologies, offering insights into the untapped potential of Thumbnails in the pursuit of comprehensive digital investigations. The findings hold implications for the forensic community and broader cybersecurity efforts, as they illuminate a pathway to unraveling the mysteries concealed within deleted multimedia on the user's computer and Android mobile devices.

articleTitle: MFTCN: A Multi-Frequency Temporal Convolutional Network for Enhancing Temperature Prediction Dependability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Accurate temperature prediction plays a key role in various fields such as agriculture, ecology, and the environment. Traditional methods directly learn historical temperature changes to predict future temperature values. However, temperature changes are complex, and traditional methods are difficult to cope with nonlinear changes in temperature, resulting in poor temperature prediction accuracy. To address this issue, we attempt to decompose complex temperature changes into several simple components and propose a multi-frequency temporal convolutional network for short-term temperature prediction. Specifically, three key modules, namely multi - frequency decomposition, component prediction, and parameter optimization are employed to reduce the complexity of temperature changes and the uncertainty of prediction while ensuring that the original temperature information is not lost. On two real temperature datasets, our proposed method outperforms five baselines, which demonstrates that decomposing complex temperature changes is beneficial to improving temperature prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: The Application of the Teaching Model of “Promoting Learning Through Competition, Promoting Teaching Through Competition” in the Course of Data Analysis and Mining
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Data Analysis and Mining is a core compulsory course for data science majors in higher education. At present, the course faces problems such as single teaching methods, limited resources, outdated experimental projects, poor applicability, and unreasonable evaluation methods, which affect the teaching quality of the course and hinder the development of talents in the field of data science. Introducing the teaching model of “Promoting Learning through Competition, Promoting Teaching through Competition” into the teaching of the Data Analysis and Mining course, integrating competition activities into the classroom, formulating practical and feasible implementation plans, actively updating teaching content and methods, improving the teaching effectiveness and quality of the Data Analysis and Miningcourse through teaching reform, and providing reference for relevant course teaching reforms. This study has been applied in practical teaching and has proven the effectiveness of this teaching model from multiple aspects.

articleTitle: Cooperative Defense-in-Depth in Large-Scale Autonomous Vehicle Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Integrating Autonomous Vehicle Networks (AVNs) into Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) presents substantial benefits for improving traffic flow, efficiency, and safety. Nevertheless, the security implications of deploying such expansive networks, particularly regarding scalability and efficiency, pose significant concerns. In response to this, cooperative defense strategies have emerged as a suitable approach for enhancing the security of AVNs. In this paper, we propose a novel, comprehensive cyber defense framework consisting of multiple decentralized and cooperative Defense-in-Depth (DiD) strategies that aim to safeguard a large-scale network like AVN by implementing multiple layers of defensive measures. Given the pivotal role of vehicular communication in the efficient functioning of AVNs, these strategies prioritize the security and integrity of the exchanged information in AVNs. An experimental analysis is presented to illustrate the efficacy of the designed DiD strategies in securing dynamic and extensive AVNs and ensuring secure and reliable communication. Additionally, we explore potential research challenges that could guide future studies to fully leverage the advantages of cooperative defense mechanisms.

articleTitle: Defect-Introducing Defect Prediction Testing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Machine learning (ML) innovations have significantly advanced the field of defect prediction in software development, offering the potential for automated error detection across vast codebases. These advancements promise to elevate software quality assurance by improving reliability and security. However, despite their benefits, existing defect prediction models are not without limitations, often failing to identify vulnerabilities or inaccurately flagging non-defective code segments as problematic. To overcome these shortcomings, this study introduces DPTester, a novel approach that diverges from traditional label-preserving transformations, aiming to more accurately mimic the complexities of real-world software development. Unlike previous methods, DPTester intentionally injects defects into source code to transform its semantics fundamentally. This methodology tests a defect prediction model's ability to identify and anticipate defects amidst semantic alterations. DPTester employs a two-step framework, consisting of automated test input and oracle generation. The initial phase generates test inputs by modifying conditional statements to induce potential defects. The subsequent phase evaluates the defect prediction models' performance using these inputs. A failure by a model to detect DPTester-introduced defects is considered an issue. Our evaluation of DPTester on two prominent defect prediction models, CodeT5+ and CodeBERT, involved the generation of 222,112 test inputs. This process demonstrated a 99% success rate in creating valid test scenarios. However, it exposed significant weaknesses in both models: CodeT5+ and CodeBERT's accuracy plummeted to 43% and 30%, respectively, when assessed against DPTester's complex test scenarios. Moreover, our analysis uncovered 144,104 and 98,574 prediction inconsistencies in CodeBERT and CodeT5+, respectively, underscoring the urgent need for model improvements to adeptly handle sophisticated testing landscapes. Furthermore, DPTester's operational efficiency-evidenced by its rapid test input generation and issue detection capabilities, averaging 0.002 seconds per test input and 0.025 seconds per issue-positions it as a valuable addition to automated testing frameworks, highlighting the necessity for advancements in defect prediction models to navigate complex testing environments effectively.

articleTitle: Adaptive Metamorphic Testing for Object Detection Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Metamorphic testing effectively mitigates the oracle problem, consequently gaining extensive utilization in the testing of machine learning systems. Present research on metamorphic testing is predominantly focused on the design and application of metamorphic relations, with scant attention to the selection and parameter configuration of metamorphic relations during the testing process to expedite fault detection. This paper presents a novel testing methodology for deep learning object detection systems, named ADRMT for Adaptive Dynamic Random Metamorphic Testing, which leverages metamorphic testing alongside dynamic random testing and adaptive random testing. By harnessing the principles of dynamic random testing to guide the selection of metamorphic relations during the testing process and the concepts of adaptive random testing for configuring the parameters of metamorphic relations, ADRMT enables the selection of metamorphic relations with superior fault detection capabilities for testing and the automated configuration of parameters, while ensuring the diversity of metamorphic relations throughout the testing process. In scenarios where testing resources are limited, this method more efficiently guides the testing process and the selection of samples for retraining.

articleTitle: Preliminary Exploration of Intelligent Virtual Avatars in the Virtual Influencer Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: The virtual avatar and Vtuber (virtual YouTube broadcaster) industries are fast-evolving sectors within today's entertainment and social media landscape. These virtual avatars are generated by software and enhanced with animation and motion capture technologies to provide interactive experiences for users. The market for virtual avatars encompasses content production and technological development, representing a significant spectrum of the digital content industry today. In the era of AI-generated content (AIGC), intelligent virtual avatars are becoming a pivotal technology in the virtual influencer domain. This study aims to preliminarily explore the applications of intelligent virtual avatars in the virtual influencer industry, particularly focusing on the positive and negative impacts after integrating artificial intelligence functionalities. Questions include whether the introduction of intelligent virtual avatars significantly enhances content creation efficiency and diversity, or whether, through AI technologies, virtual influencers can achieve more real-time interactions and more closely mimic human response patterns, thus enhancing audience immersion and loyalty. The introduction of AI technology is notably evident in real-time interactions with audiences. Moreover, intelligent virtual avatars can produce content continuously, unrestricted by physical or emotional states, offering a production advantage. However, the use of related technologies, including speech synthesis, also initiates a series of negative impacts, posing a threat to the job security of human creators. As virtual avatars can produce content more cost-effectively and efficiently, human creators might find their skills and experiences less rare, potentially affecting their career prospects and earnings. Additionally, intelligent virtual avatars may foster the proliferation of lower-quality content, as they can quickly produce large amounts of material without deep creativity or cultural sensitivity, potentially leading to content homogenization, reducing cultural diversity and the depth of creativity. This study employs a qualitative approach, interviewing two well-known companies in Taiwan that utilize AIGC technology for virtual influencers or virtual avatars. The questions cover three aspects: 1. Whether AI applications in virtual avatars can enhance the industry's business models, 2. Whether AI can accelerate the existing digital content production process, 3. Whether the inclusion of AI reduces company manpower. The introduction of intelligent virtual avatars has a significant impact on the virtual influencer industry, bringing both positive effects in promoting industry development and innovation, and potential negative impacts on the creative labor market. This study attempts to find a balance between these opportunities and challenges needed for industry development.

articleTitle: Image Tampering Detection Method Based on Multi-Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Currently, with the continuous advancement of deep learning technology, numerous neural network-based image tampering detection models have emerged, achieving promising detection results. Traditional algorithms based on handcrafted features are gradually being replaced. However, these models often exhibit unstable detection accuracy for different types of tampered images due to their reliance on feature extraction techniques like filters and constrained convolutions. Furthermore, these models generally lack generalization capability and fail to detect previously unseen types of tampering. In recent years, emerging technologies such as attention mechanisms have been widely applied and researched in the field of image processing. Attention mechanisms allow models to focus on critical parts of an image, specifically the tampered regions, significantly improving the accuracy of image tampering detection tasks. To address the aforementioned issues and enhance model detection accuracy, this thesis proposes a multi-feature fusion network based on attention mechanisms. An adaptive feature extraction module is designed to integrate image RGB, noise, and edge information, applying attention mechanisms in both spatial and channel dimensions. This attention-guided enhanced neural network enables the spontaneous learning of tampering features, facilitating the detection of various types of tampering. Additionally, a low-level pixel branch is incorporated to enable the network to notice tampering traces in low-level texture information, further improving detection accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared to existing detection models, the proposed model not only achieves superior detection accuracy but also exhibits greater robustness.

articleTitle: A New Improved Method of Recurrent Memory Perception for Radar Echo Extrapolation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Precipitation forecasting has long been a prominent topic in meteorology, as accurate predictions of impending rainfall are crucial for daily life and travel planning. Currently, radar echo extrapolation serves as the primary method for precipitation proximity forecasting. The precision of extrapolated radar echo maps directly impacts the ability of weather forecasters to successfully anticipate severe weather events. Deep learning techniques have recently gained widespread adoption in this domain, enabling the identification of precipitation events with varying intensities. However, existing approaches primarily focus on capturing long-term motion dynamics through recurrent neural networks. As a result, these methods struggle to accurately capture the trends in radar echo motion as the prediction time horizon increases, leading to issues such as feature disappearance and blurring in the predicted radar echo maps. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a novel recurrent unit called RM-ConvLSTM. This unit incorporates a recurrent memory perception module and an additional memory component to enhance the model's performance in long-term radar echo map predictions. The real-world CIKM 2017 radar echo dataset is utilized to evaluate the proposed method and to conduct comparative experiments with representative models from previous studies. The results demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms existing methods in predicting radar image quality.

articleTitle: Towards an Evaluation Methodology of ML Systems from the Perspective of Robustness and Data Quality
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: A significant surge of innovations and new implementations now hinges on advanced AI-based systems. To foster trust in artificial intelligence systems, it is imperative to address the current lack of a structured approach to assess these systems. An evaluation methodology for AI is of paramount importance, especially for implementation in safety-critical applications. This paper is an initial step toward establishing a framework for the evaluation methodology of ML systems. We propose incorporating a multi-property assessment of an ML model and state the different building blocks that can facilitate the compliance of AI systems for developers as well as certification authorities. We demonstrate the implementation of the proposed framework for the evaluation of ML systems, one by assessing the robustness property, and two by assessing the data quality property of dataset used for ML model. In assessing the robustness property of the ML model through adversarial attacks, we use the implementation of the CW attack for an LSTM model trained on the OpenSky dataset. For data quality assessment, we evaluate data consistency through the implementation of outlier detection algorithms. We illustrate our results on the OpenSky dataset and highlight the challenges involved in assessing the robustness of deep neural networks.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence as a New Engine for Boosting Economic Performance of Manufacturing Enterprises
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology is reshaping the operational models and competitive advantages of enterprises, garnering significant attention. The development of AI is not just a scientific and technological revolution but also the core driving force for a new wave of industrial change. This study examines how AI technology can improve the economic performance of Chinese manufacturing enterprises.
