Based on a large dataset of27, 133 valid observations from 3,434 Chinese enterprises between 2007 and 2022, the findings show that a 1 unit increase in AI technology application leads to a 6.59% increase in corporate economic performance in the current year, 6.96% in the following year, and 7.33% in the third year. This indicates that AI technology has a delayed yet gradually improving impact on enhancing corporate economic performance. This study confirms that corporate solvency moderates the relationship between AI technology and corporate economic performance. Moreover, AI technology has a significant positive impact on the economic performance of non-high-tech enterprises and those located in both eastern and western regions. This study contributes to AI research in the Chinese context and provides recommendations for Chinese government and manufacturing enterprise managers to enhance corporate economic performance.

articleTitle: The Battle of Ethics in Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: With autonomous cars promising a comfortable and efficient driving experience, it is of paramount importance to ensure they can replicate or do better than the human decision-making process. However, some decisions are more than a combination of mathematics, they require a sense of ethics, which poses a significant challenge in attempting to encode it into algorithms for computers to adhere to. The ethical considerations surrounding autonomous vehicles have garnered significant attention in recent years, specifically in regard to consequences in which human harm is unavoidable. What actions should be taken by an autonomous vehicle when it's faced with an inevitable collision? Furthermore, who should be responsible for determining the most acceptable course of action for the vehicle to take? Given the probability of pedestrians facing greater harm than passengers in autonomous vehicle accidents, particularly in regions with substantial pedestrian traffic like Botswana and India, a survey was conducted to explore the ethical inclinations of sub-populations within these countries. Recently large language models (LLMs) have shown to generate answers with logical reasoning under provided contexts. Various methods have been proposed for utilizing LLMs in autonomous driving, making it crucial to examine the ethical decision-making tendencies of prominent LLMs. Being human means you are biased to a certain extent but is that the case with LLMs as well? This paper presents the survey results of sub-populations from Botswana and India alongside examining the ethical decision-making tendencies of large language models.

articleTitle: Reshaping and Transforming of English Teaching in Higher Education in the ChatGPT Era: An Empirical Study Based on Big Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) technology advances, ChatGPT, a cutting-edge natural language processing technique, is increasingly being integrated into various domains, including education. This chatbot, powered by a robust large-scale language model, showcases AI capabilities to the general public. To investigate the impact of ChatGPT on English language education at the tertiary level, this study employs bibliometric analysis and CiteSpace to visually map 844 relevant academic papers from the Web of Science database. Through big data analysis of existing literature, this study synthesizes the research landscape and identifies key trends by examining article quantity, keyword frequency, collaborative patterns among countries, and citation frequency of influential literature. Global scholarly interest in the educational impact of ChatGPT is growing, with diverse research perspectives. The existing literature on the impact of ChatGPT on English language education in higher education is limited. In light of ChatGPT's positive impact on English language proficiency among higher education students, future researchers should explore its implications for advancing English language education from various perspectives. There is an urgent need to discuss the benefits and challenges of using ChatGPT in English language teaching in higher education. Building on current scholarly achievements, future research should focus on enhancing personalized English instruction, intelligent assessment methods, and streamlined knowledge retrieval systems in higher education.

articleTitle: Blockchain Implementation for Visual Art Copyright Protection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: As digitization continues to grow, the distribution of creative work has become more widespread. However, this has also led to an increase in copyright infringement, which poses a significant threat to rights holders. Traditional copyright exchange platforms face various challenges, such as inefficiencies, high transaction costs, compromised personal privacy, and safety risks regarding data. To address these issues, we propose a new system for protecting the copyright of visual artwork using Hyperledger technology. Our approach involves using the SIFT algorithm to compute feature vectors from visuals. If the similarity exceeds specified thresholds, the system flags the infringements and initiates punitive measures. On the other hand, if the similarity falls below the threshold, the system saves an imperceptible watermark embedded within the visual on IPFS as a safeguard against plagiarism. Our system benefits from blockchain's unique attributes, such as scalability, storage efficacy, and quick transmission. This strengthens the system's defenses against potential vulnera-bilities. Empirical studies confirm our system's effectiveness in recognizing similarities and defending copyrights. Further-more, the blockchain-backed copyright registration process ensures the portability and traceability of copyright data, providing a secure and effective solution for protecting visual artwork copyrights.

articleTitle: Generating Evaluation Criteria of Domain-Specific Large Language Model Using Word Vector Clustering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: In recent years, the use of large language models for domain-specific tasks has gained increasing attention. However, the performance of current domain-specific large language models tends to be assessed through manual evaluation, which limits the broader application of this technology. Addressing the limitations of existing methods for evaluating domain-specific large language models, we introduce a frame-work capable of generating evaluation criteria from multiple perspectives using large language models. This framework elicits a plethora of candidate outcomes from large language models through multi-turn dialogues. It employs word vector clustering methods to eliminate outliers caused by hallucination issues, thereby identifying the most valuable generated results. We illustrate our approach by applying it to financial and legal consulting tasks. Through experimentation, we identify the dimensionality reduction and clustering methods that yield optimal performance in these tasks. An experiment demonstrated the process of this framework, proving its feasibility. The results indicate that our framework is capable of effectively generating comprehensive evaluation criteria, providing guidance for further testing of Domain-Specific Large Language Models.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Functional ETL Testing Methodologies for Real-World Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: In today's data-driven enterprises, data warehouses are crucial for aggregating diverse datasets for analysis and research. The ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) process is central to this, involving data extraction, integration, cleansing, and loading into the warehouse. Challenges in ETL can cause inaccuracies, diminishing the value of high-quality source data. Robust ETL testing methodologies are essential to ensure correct implementation and efficient execution. This paper surveys existing functional ETL testing approaches, categorizing them into data quality and balancing tests. Data quality tests identify issues like missing values and outliers in the target data, while balancing tests verify data consistency between source and target. The research highlights unresolved challenges in completeness and scalability, proposes future research directions, and includes an empirical study of ETL testing on the Our World in Data warehouse, identifying data disparities and abnormalities.

articleTitle: An Empirical Study on the Characteristics of Connected Knowledge Subgraphs on Stack Overflow
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: In the Stack Overflow (SO) community, users typically employ links (including internal and external links) in their posts or comments to better present their cited knowledge. Prior studies have already demonstrated that external links bring valuable information, thus enhancing the software engineering knowledge quality within the community. Nowadays, the act of users referencing internal links has formed connected knowledge subgraphs with question threads as nodes and internal links as edges. However, the characteristics of the subgraphs have not been investigated. It is still unclear how and why users reference internal links within the subgraphs. In addition, the impact of internal links within the subgraphs on the community is yet to be explored. Therefore, we constructed subgraphs through internal links and analyzed their structural stability based on the official SO data dump. Subsequently, we employed qualitative analysis methods to explore how and why developers reference internal links within the subgraphs. Finally, we conducted a quantitative analysis to assess the impact of the subgraphs on the community. We observed the subgraphs are structurally stable, with a slowing expansion rate. Meanwhile, We found that 82.4% of links were cited without summarizing the content. Notably, 64.3% of links without summaries are likely to hinder knowledge comprehension once they become obsolete. This is especially pronounced for links cited for “providing solutions to subproblem”, reaching as high as 96.9%. Our quantitative analysis has uncovered the last updated time of question threads within the subgraphs is closer to the present. Simultaneously, they also exhibit a lower deletion rate. Based on our findings, we provide actionable suggestions for developers, SO community, and researchers. For example, we encourage researchers to develop a visualization tool that can visualize question threads and their internal links from the “linked” list as graphs. This facilitates in-depth exploration of specific software engineering topics.

articleTitle: Predictive Mutation-Based Fault Localization: Balancing Effectiveness and Cost
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Mutation-Based Fault Localization (MBFL) can provide high FL accuracy in localizing faults because of the abundant information provided by the execution of the test suite in a large number of mutants. Nevertheless, its exorbitant execution cost renders it challenging for practical adoption. Traditional reduction strategies reduce costs by sampling mutants or mutation operators at the expense of sacrificing fault localization accuracy. In this paper, we propose a novel MBFL technique using predictive-based execution information, PMBFL, which reduces the execution cost while retaining high accuracy in localizing faults. PMBFL firstly captures dependencies between changes in program behavior (i.e. mutants) and test results (i.e., pass or fail) via the learning model. It then predicts the execution information of each test on a given mutant, instead of reducing the number of mutants, to reduce the execution cost. The empirical study on 176 faulty programs from Defects4J (2.0.0) shows that PMBFL can significantly reduce the execution cost by 70% while maintaining high fault localization accuracy.

articleTitle: Finite Time-Based Adaptive Terminal Sliding Mode Fault-Tolerant Control for Port Automated Guided Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: This paper designs a new Finite-Time Adaptive Terminal Sliding Mode (FTATSM) control scheme, specifically designed for Automated Guided Vehicles (AGVs) engaged in port silo-clearing operations. This method combines a novel dynamic terminal sliding surface with a super-twisting reaching law to significantly enhance the AGV's rapid response to dynamic operational demands. Utilizing the norm of the state error to capture dynamic trends as a terminal sliding mode convergence adjustment mechanism, this paper develops a novel dynamic terminal sliding surface for finite-time convergence during the sliding phase. The integration of the super-twisting law effectively mitigates the common chattering phenomenon in sliding mode control, substantially improving both the convergence speed of the terminal sliding mode and its smoothness. Moreover, the design incorporates robust adaptive technology, successfully addressing external disturbances and bias faults, thereby significantly enhancing the stability and safety of AGVs trajectory tracking. The FTATSM control method is tailor-made for complex silo-clearing environments such as ports, warehouses, and cargo areas, not only boosting the intelligence and efficiency of AGV systems but also enhancing their emergency response capabilities, ensuring robust performance even under uncertain conditions. This approach represents a significant advance in the design of industrial automation fault-tolerant control systems, offering substantial improvements in operational safety and efficiency.

articleTitle: A Privacy Leakage Detection Method for Personalized Course Recommendation Based on Pi-Calculus
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Privacy protection is one of the main approaches to improve the security and reliability of personalized course recommendation systems. However, the current privacy protection methods for personalized course recommendation mainly focus on data protection, but ignore the potential privacy leakage that may be caused by the system behavior. In addition, privacy protection is not fully considered in the initial phases of system development and design. To address this issue, this paper presents a methodology for detecting privacy leakage in personalized course recommendation systems using the process algebra Pi-Calculus. Firstly, the basic semantics and evolution rules of Pi-Calculuss as well as the definition of mutual simulation techniques are introduced. Then the personalized course recommendation system is mapped to a process algebra Pi-Calculus, a formal description and analysis of the interaction behavior of the components of the personalized course recommendation system is given, and finally a framework for privacy leakage detection is introduced and applied to a case study to detect whether there is privacy leakage behavior in the recommendation system by the inter-simulation technique. Experiments demonstrate that the method can effectively detect potential privacy leakage problems in the early stages of system development.

articleTitle: Enhancing Traffic Safety at Unsignalized Intersections Through Constraint-Chain Based Cooperative Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: The cooperative driving strategy at intersections encompasses both macroscopic (sequence level) and microscopic (motion level) perspectives. However, few studies have integrated both aspects, resulting in ineffective and unsafe execution of macroscopic decisions at the microscopic level. This paper presents a constraint chain framework that addresses both aspects by transforming the complex conflict relationships into executable motion constraints. The solution to multi-vehicle coordination problem is thus divided into three steps: determining the passing sequence, establishing the constraint chain, and setting up the distributed vehicle dynamics control. A constraint-following control algorithm is proposed to ensure each vehicle adheres to its designated constraints. Unlike previous algorithms, the proposed cooperative driving strategy eliminates the need for conflict mediation and velocity planning. Rigorous simulations have been conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed strategy. Results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm increases the average minimum speed compared to baseline methods, resulting in steadier traffic flow and improved energy efficiency.

articleTitle: Industrial Process Fault Detection with Multi-View Feature Fusion Attention Mechanism Assisted Autoencoder Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Fault detection technology plays a crucial role in ensuring the safety and efficiency of industrial processes. Industrial processes are subject to changing operating conditions, causing their characteristics to evolve over time and exhibit dynamic, non-Gaussian, and non-linear behaviors in the data. Unfortunately, existing research in process monitoring often fails to address these properties simultaneously, leading to unsatisfactory fault detection outcomes. To address this gap, a novel fault detection framework is introduced in this study, leveraging a Multi-View Feature Fusion At-tention Mechanism Assisted Autoencoder Network (MFA-AE). To capture the dynamic and non-Gaussian features of industrial processes comprehensively, slow feature analysis and independent component analysis are initially employed to extract features separately from the raw data. Subsequently, an attention mechanism is integrated to fuse these extracted features with the raw data, enhancing the information available for subsequent modeling. These integrated features are then passed through the Autoencoder (AE) network, where non-linear features are further explored, and a fault detection model is constructed based on the residuals of the AE network. To assess the effectiveness and feasibility of the MFA-AE approach, experiments are conducted using the Tennessee Eastman process. The results affirm the superiority of the proposed method over state-of-the-art techniques in terms of detection accuracy, demonstrating the promising potential of the MFA-AE scheme for enhancing fault detection in industrial processes.

articleTitle: Constraint-Following Robust Control for Flying Car: A Model-Based Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: The design of flying car control presents significant challenges in performing transportation tasks in complex environments, particularly in challenging terrains such as urban three-dimensional traffic. This paper addresses the intricate control challenges encountered by flying cars during transportation missions, with the primary objective of enabling efficient navigation within designated safe areas and seamless adaptation to various environments. A robust control method is proposed for the analytical model of flying car dynamics, which encompasses a novel control framework involving differential homeomorphism transformation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\eth$</tex>, construction of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\zeta$</tex> - transformation, introduction of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta-\text{measure}$</tex> and the design of a robust controller. The innovative control strategies proposed, including constraint design, robustness and constraint following, empower the flying car to demonstrate safety and reliability while autonomously completing tasks and enhancing operational efficiency in demanding environments.

articleTitle: Effects of $\boldsymbol{L}_{\boldsymbol{p}}$-norm Deficits in Quantization Human Perception on Attack Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: The majority of adversarial attack methods aim to enhance the quality of adversarial samples by decreasing the perceived distance between the adversarial samples and the original samples. However, the majority of these methods still accomplish this by restricting the size of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{\mathrm{p}}-\text{norm}$</tex>. On the other hand, we discover that the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{\mathrm{p}}-\text{norm}$</tex> is inconsistent with the perceived similarity based on the literature and experiments. Crucially, we also prove that “Potential Adversarial Samples” exist. This result suggests that there is still room for improvement in the attack success rate and query efficiency of the current <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{\mathrm{p}}-\text{based}$</tex> attack methods, and the quantity of “Potential Adversarial Samples” can be utilized as an indicator to assess the attack methods' optimizable space. The discovery also offers a precise course and objective for the optimization of attack methods in the following years. Furthermore, we have derived seven image quality assessment metrics from literature research. We then weigh the benefits and drawbacks of each index against the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{2}$</tex> norm in terms of human perception, and as one of the optimization goals of our next attack strategy, we choose the indexes that most closely match human perception.

articleTitle: A Model-Agnostic Interpretability Approach Based on Enhanced Hierarchical Clustering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: The Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME) is a relatively novel technique for explaining black-box models. LIME generates perturbed instances of the model based on a random instance, and then approximates the original model with a linear model derived from the weighted perturbed instances, thereby providing an explanation for individual predictions. While LIME effectively addresses the opacity of black-box models, the randomness in instance generation often leads to unstable and inaccurate predictions. For a given prediction, different explanations may be generated, posing critical issues, particularly in security-sensitive domains. In response to these challenges, we propose a stable version of LIME, named DDLIME(Density and Distance-based LIME). DDLIME leverages improved hierarchical clustering and KNN algorithms to select instances that are most similar to the data, thus reducing the impact of perturbations. Additionally, the enhanced hierarchical clustering, incorporating density and distance metrics, enables DDLIME to address the limitations of traditional hierarchical clustering in clustering non-spherical clusters. Consequently, DDLIME can effectively capture complex structures and patterns within the data. The experimental results on three binary public datasets from the UCI repository demonstrate that DDLIME provides more stable explanations compared to LIME. Furthermore, compared to both baseline models, DDLIME exhibits superior performance across various evaluation metrics.

articleTitle: Performance Profiling of Federated Learning Across Heterogeneous Mobile Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: As mobile devices increasingly become more widely used in data analytics and machine learning, Federated Learning (FL) offers a promising decentralised approach that maintains data privacy and reduces data transmission costs. This work analyses FL performance across heterogeneous mobile devices in real deployment. We examine the impacts of device heterogeneity on the training efficiency of FL systems by conducting a series of experiments involving real and emulated smartphones with various computational capabilities and network conditions. Through performance profiling, we identify bottlenecks in mobile settings to overcome the unique challenges mobile environments pose and design an FL system that effectively uses heterogeneous devices. Our experiments make use of a federated CIFAR10 dataset. Our results indicate higher setup times on physical devices than emulated ones, regardless of the network connection type. While data loading from storage is the primary bottleneck, consuming up to 88% of setup time, with a Broadband connection, downloading the model from the server becomes another major bottleneck with a 4G/LTE connection. Our findings also reveal that the fit function of the training phase takes up to 94% of training time. These insights can hopefully aid in designing FL systems that adapt effectively to heterogeneous resources in FL environments.

articleTitle: A Review of the Applications of Heuristic Algorithms in Test Case Generation Problem
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: This paper reviews the state-of-the-art heuristic-based methods in test case generation, analyzing the technical characteristics of these technologies. By conducting a thorough analysis, the study categorizes these methods into distinct types based on their underlying principles. It explains the core concepts of each category, as well as its methods, and provides an overview of their main applications in test case generation. Additionally, the study also explores areas that have not been adequately researched in the current literature and offers prospects for future research directions. The objective of this paper is to provide a comprehensive and systematic overview of current research and to offer valuable insights and guidance for future research and best practices on heuristic-based method for test case generation.

articleTitle: QAQA-SS: An Improved Fuzzing Approach with Seed Scheduling Based on the UCB Algorithm for QA Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Question Answering (QA) system is a type of artificial intelligence application designed to comprehend natural language questions and provide accurate, meaningful natural language answers. However, there are errors in the QA system, which can cause inconvenience for users and even lead to economic losses and security issues. In response to these challenges, QAQA showed up. QAQA designs several metamorphic relations (MRs) and achieves precise automatic testing through semantic-guided search and enhanced test oracles. However, QAQA fairly selects each seed (initial test input) in sequential order and assigns them a fixed number of mutations, which leaves many seeds that could produce quality test inputs neglected. This paper proposes an improved version named QAQA-SS (QAQA-Seed Schedule), where we enhance QAQA with a seed scheduling module and a fuzzing framework featuring iterative feedback. We combine the Upper Confidence Bound (UCB) algorithm with perplexity to devise a novel seed scheduling algorithm. QAQA-SS selects superior seeds and allocates appropriate mutation counts (energy) to generate more error-inducing test inputs within a limited energy budget. Additionally, we introduce a text paraphrasing operation to improve the performance of finding errors in the QA system. We conducted experiments following the experimental setup of QAQA on three datasets: BoolQ, SQuAD2, and NarrativeQA. Our experimental results reveal a noteworthy enhancement in the error discovery rate for QAQA-SS, achieving 81,777 error discoveries compared to 64,354 error discoveries with QAQA.

articleTitle: Research on the Utilization of Cloud Anchors in 5G Mobile Networks for Interactive Augmented Reality Display and Sculptural Art
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: In recent years, Augmented Reality (AR) technology has seen widespread adoption in museum art displays, progressing from AR markers to AR SLAM, and now to the emerging trend of AR Cloud Anchor with the advent of 5G mobile networks. AR Cloud Anchor, a crucial component of this third generation of AR, allows for the synchronized display of AR virtual objects by sharing anchors in the cloud, offering innovative possibilities beyond traditional standalone AR experiences. Despite its potential, there are limited cases of AR Cloud Anchor implementation in art exhibitions. This research focuses on the technical application of AR Cloud Anchor in art exhibitions, specifically utilizing sculptures as the medium. The study's design encompasses four main aspects: the process of 3D scanning for sculptures, defining AR anchors for the sculpture medium, creator experience design, and user interaction design. The research aims to provide insights into the technical implementation of AR Cloud Anchor, offering valuable information on data storage, the artistic impact of augmented sculptures, and user preferences for AR applications extended by Cloud Anchor technology. Preliminary conclusions suggest that AR Cloud Anchor technology brings significant innovation to art exhibitions, enhancing audience engagement and making exhibitions more attractive and participatory. Additionally, there is a correlation between users' AR technology experiences and their perceptions of app usability and AR technology's impact on art exhibitions, highlighting the importance of user education and experience in promoting AR technology. Users also express interest in the intervention of virtual sculptures in public spaces, indicating substantial potential for AR technology in enriching artistic experiences.

articleTitle: ADS Modeling and Safety Verification in Extreme Driving Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Autonomous vehicles play a vital role in improving traffic efficiency and reducing traffic accidents. The spatio-temporal data in driving scenarios is complex and unpredictable, with uncertain interaction behavior. Despite efforts by developers to model road dynamics for evaluating Autonomous Driving Systems (ADS), safety concerns under accidental and catastrophic road conditions have been overlooked. Firstly, to tackle this, this paper proposes extending feature variables for catastrophic scenarios using Domain-Specific Modeling Language (DSML). Introducing the Accidental and Catastrophic Automatic Driving Scenario Modeling Language (AC-ADSML) aims to accurately model ADS behavior in accidental and catastrophic road conditions. The AC-ADSML meta-model categorizes scenario variables and specifies abstract and concrete syntax along with operational semantics. Secondly, it is then transformed into Networks of Stochastic Hybrid Automata (NSHA) following ATL rules. The CARLA simulator is employed to replicate urban driving scenarios during natural disasters with PCTL scenario specifications. Model security can be verified using UPP AAL-SMC. Finally, an autonomous vehicle with adaptive cruise control is used as an example to verify the safety of the proposed model under different road condition parameters.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis Using Channelized Encoder-Decoder Frame for Distributed Redundant Inertial Navigation System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Device redundancy measurement systems (DRMS) are gaining popularity in most industrial scenarios. In the area of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), DRMS can provide measurement data from various maneuvering channels and increase the reliability of upper level systems notably. Most fault diagnosis studies for DRMS treat a single device as the basic fault diagnosis unit and assume that the sensitivity centers of multiple devices are the same. However, the distributed redundant inertial navigation systems (DRINS) on UAVs are dominated by three-channel state characteristics, which amplifies the complexity of obtained data and needs more detailed fault diagnosis approaches. What's more, devices in the DRINS have different sensitivity centers, which means much more spatial information needs to be considered for fault diagnosis. To cope with the aforementioned problems, we present a Channelized Encoder-Decoder (CED) framework in this paper to achieve the fault diagnosis for DRINS on UAVs. In CED framework, the basic fault diagnosis unit is refined into each channel, and the data captured by DRINS is cross correlated according to different channels and different measurement devices. The data-driven strategy using deep learning methods is integrated to realize the feature self-extraction of channelized data and the self-determination of fault location. The feasibility of CED is verified through extensive experiments including comparison with other methods. It is validated that, after parameter fine-tuning, CED frame can achieve fairly accurate fault location results when faced with multi-channel and multi-device failures, providing an inspiring way for UAV DRINS fault diagnosis.

articleTitle: An Empirical Study on Modeling Testing Requirements for Safety-Critical Software
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: The use of model-based techniques for the development and testing of safety-critical software is a current research focus. However, the complete and accurate depiction of software safety attributes during model construction remains a problem that needs to be addressed. This study focuses on the integration of safety features in model-based testing technologies for safety-critical software. By using the MARTE modeling language and traditional as well as innovative safety analysis methods, this study demonstrates the evolution from basic to advanced models through an empirical project. The empirical results indicate that the analysis outcomes obtained through traditional safety methods (FMEA and FHA) can be modeled in the MARTE language through the extension of constructs or addition of stereotypes. The systematic safety analysis method (STPA) can utilize MARTE to extend the viewpoint layer, resulting in a new hybrid model. This facilitates a better realization of the depiction of software safety attributes based on models and provides a more robust technical foundation for automated modeling.

articleTitle: Using $\mu \text{Bert}$ to Improve Mutation-Based Fault Localization for Novice Programs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Programming learning has emerged as a prevalent trend. However, due to their lack of experience, novices often encounter difficulties in effectively debugging programs. To address the challenges faced by novices in programming, the development of automatic program fault localization presents a potential solution. Nonetheless, the majority of existing fault localization methods prove inadequate for novice-level programs, with the two predominant approaches being mutation-based fault localization (MBFL) and spectrum-based fault localization(SBFL). The SBFL may falter, particularly with novice programs failing to clear any tests, which restricts its utility. Meanwhile, the MBFL doesn't fully account for the gap between simulated mutants and real faults, often covering just a fragment of actual issues. This results in reduced fault localization efficiency and higher operational costs, underscoring the challenges each method faces in various situations. To overcome this obstacle, this study proposes a novel fault localization method for novice programs, termed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathbf{Bert}$</tex> Mutation-Based Novice Fault Localization <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mu \mathbf{MB}- \mathbf{NFL})$</tex>. This method introduces a new type of mutant, which, by integrating contextual information, first generates a mask at the statement level within the source code, and subsequently produces a token for the segment of the mask most likely to simulate an actual failure. These mutants are referred to as Neural-mutants. Within this methodology, we incorporate the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathbf{Bert}$</tex> tool, based on the CodeBERT model, to conduct mutation testing, substituting traditional mutants with the newly generated Neural-mutants for fault localization in novice programs. To evaluate the feasibility of the approach, experiments are conducted on 182 fault codes from novice programmers, using SBFL and MBFL as benchmarks. The experimental outcomes demonstrate that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathbf{MB}- \mathbf{NFL}$</tex> surpasses the other two methods in terms of localization precision. Specifically, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathbf{MB-NFL}$</tex> achieves localization for 51, 115, and 142 in the three indicators of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$TOP - N (N=1,3,5)$</tex>, respectively.

articleTitle: Research on Program Change Impact Analysis Methods Based on Software Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the current program change impact analysis methods have coarse calculation granularity and without considering the actual situation of program change, results in overstating the impact propagation range and inability to quantify the degree of change impact, this paper proposes a program change impact analysis method based on the software network. Firstly, by combining the complex network theory to characterize the structural attributes and evolution patterns of software system, we abstract the software network morphology of system; Secondly, basing on the type of program change and the actual propagation of change impacts, two concepts of impact propagation decay rate and minimum threshold for impact marking are introduced to construct the simulation sub-model of impact propagation processes, enabling the analysis of the propagation range of program impacts; Thirdly, according to the structural properties of software network and the intrinsic attributes of nodes, the ripple degree simulation sub-model is constructed, and five quantization factors of the node's influenced degree are given to complete the quantitative assignment of the node's influenced degree; Finally, several open source software is used for application verification. Experimental results show that the proposed method aligns with reality in analyzing the propagation range of program change impacts, thus scientifically and reasonably reflecting the ripple effects of change impacts within the software system. At the same time, the method accurately and effectively quantifies the impact of program changes on other parts, thereby providing theoretical support for change impact analysis in software engineering.

articleTitle: Soft Actor-Critic Based Anti-Attack XSS Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks have become increasingly prevalent and sophisticated with the rapid development of Internet technology, posing a severe threat to network security. Deep learning-based XSS detection models autonomously learn complex features and pat-terns, boosting accuracy and adaptability. However, they often fail to detect novel and sophisticated adversarial tactics, leading to significant security breaches. To coun-teract these limitations, this study propose a novel Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) based anti-attack XSS detection. Our method enhances decision-making robustness by leveraging maximum entropy principles, thereby increasing the randomness and unpredictability of strategy selection. Additionally, we propose a unique Agent-Environment interaction framework specifically designed for XSS de-tection, which significantly improves the model's learning efficiency and adaptability. Comprehensive experimental validations demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms existing methods in detecting a variety of XSS attack scenarios, particularly against unknown and complex attack patterns, thereby exhibiting enhanced adaptability and robustness.

articleTitle: A Survey of Automatic Driving Environment Perception
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Driven by new generation AI technologies such as big data, cloud computing and machine learning, autonomous driving has been significantly developed and progressed in recent years. Among the core technologies of autonomous driving, environment perception, as one of them, simulates the visual perception ability of the human eye to enable vehicles to recognize and understand the surrounding environment, thereby achieving safe and efficient driving. However, autonomous driving faces numerous challenges in practical applications, such as the impact of adverse weather on the quality of visual images, the accuracy problem of visual recognition and so on. To solve these problems, scholars have carried out a large amount of research work. This review will comprehensively sort out the research results in the above related fields, aiming to provide readers with a comprehensive view of machine vision technology and perception technology in autonomous vehicles, and explore its future development trend and possible challenges. We will introduce the basic concepts and key technologies of autonomous driving perception, and discuss various advanced perception methods and their applications in detail. Finally, we will look forward to the future development trend of autonomous driving perception technology, which can provide reference for further promoting the development of autonomous driving technology and is of practical significance for researchers and practitioners.

articleTitle: CGFuzz: A Dynamic Test Case Generation Method for DL Framework Based on Function Coverage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Deep neural networks have gradually become the cornerstone technology to promote progress in various security fields, and deep learning frameworks are the basis for constructing neural networks. Even minor flaws in a deep learning framework as few as a few lines of code can lead to widespread failures in the model, posing a significant threat to the security of the system. Software testing is an effective means to mine the defects of deep learning framework. The defects originating from the underlying functions of the framework's source code can precipitate problems across all APIs that invoke these functions. This study directs its focus towards the examination of low-level function coverage and proposes an efficient API test case generation technique predicated on the guidance of the coverage. We define the number of low-level functions covered by the execution procedure as a test adequacy metric. At the same time, the method for tracing low-level functions correlated with APIs is proposed, so as to calculate the coverage metric. Based on the completely random generation of API test cases, the coverage is used to guide the seed weight update, so as to optimize the test case selection strategy. Besides, the fuzzy rule selection strategy will be adjusted to perform targeted fuzzy mutation on the selected test cases, leading to efficient test cases which cover more low-level functions. Experimental results underscore the efficacy of our method in generating test cases with enhanced coverage effects, thereby introducing novel methods and concepts for the quality assurance of deep learning frameworks.

articleTitle: Design and Application of Ship Information System Development Platform Architecture Based on OSGi
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Military software generalization, serialization, modularization is the trend of software development in military enterprises. This paper proposes a set of high real-time, loosely coupled plug-in ship information system development platform based on OSGi (Open Services Gateway initiative) standard. The platform adopts a dynamically configurable plug-in architecture, provides a stable kernel with plug-in management, plug-in communication, plug-in extension and other functions as the core, provides system plug-ins based on the main interface, logs, multi-style, multi-language and other functions, and provides auxiliary tools such as development wizards, dynamic layouts, deployment tools and so on. The platform reduces the coupling between plug-ins, improves the flexibility and adaptability of plug-in applications, and facilitates secondary development. Through the application of shipboard radar integrated display software, it fully verifies the feasibility of the platform's application in ship information system with high efficiency, high reliability and high performance.

articleTitle: Advancing Forensic Examination of Cyber Predator Communication Through Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: By analyzing textual and behavioral patterns in online conversations, machine learning algorithms can assist forensic investigators in identifying potential predators, understanding their strategies, and ultimately enhancing the protection of vulnerable individuals. The importance of digital evidence cannot be overstated because digital evidence is often the key to proving the guilt or innocence of someone for actions for which they have been charged when accused of committing a digital crime. The prevalence of criminal activity on social media sites is often very difficult to determine since there are currently no comprehensive statistics on social media crimes. This increased rate of social media crimes has led to an increasing need for social network forensics. Current digital forensic techniques and tools can also not detect patterns efficiently among large datasets from social media and other online digital domains. Artificial intelligence and natural language processing have been seen as solutions to these problems encountered by forensics experts. The research focuses on the development of a robust machine-learning model capable of distinguishing patterns among suspected predatory conversations, thereby offering a proactive approach to combating online sexual exploitation. This study contributes to the ongoing efforts to create safer digital spaces by unveiling the hidden truths embedded in textual content. The findings hold significant implications for developing effective preventive measures, fostering a more secure online environment, and safeguarding individuals from potential harm.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach for Software Defect Prediction Through Relational Association Rules Based on Cost-Sensitive Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Software defect prediction (SDP) can predict software modules with potential defect risks before software testing, thereby optimizing the allocation of testing resources. Relational association rules can characterize the relations between data attributes and reveal relevant patterns in complex data. We propose a software defect prediction model using relational association rules based on cost-sensitive learning (CSLRAR). To address the inherent class-imbalance problem of defect data, CSLRAR employs one-class classification strategy to separately mine relational association rules for the defective class and non-defective class using Apriori. Furthermore, we use all training data to construct a feature relational association rule selection mechanism, which which serves as the basis for defective relational association rules set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(RAR_{+})$</tex> and non-defective relational association rules set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(RAR_{-})$</tex> to determine whether the rule is retained. The feature relational association rule selection mechanism can improve the quality of the rules set obtained during the rule generation stage. In addition, we conducted experimental evaluations on nine publicly available datasets from the PROMISE database. By comparing and analyzing five baseline models, it has been proven that CSLRAR is significantly better than the baseline in terms of Balance, MCC, and Gmean.

articleTitle: Complex Network Theory-based Deep Neural Network Degradation Analysis in the Context of Bit Attack
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: The reliability of deep learning technologies has become an unavoidable issue due to their application in safety-critical domains. In addition to the well-known adversarial examples, bit attacks hijack the execution of functions and pose threats to the models. Therefore, we propose a degradation analysis framework leveraging complex network theory for the first time to comprehend the impact of bit attacks on deep neural networks. Within the framework, a bit attack simulator and a structural-functional (S-F) network analyzer are developed. The bit attack simulator obtains erroneous models through training, quantization, and bit flipping. And the structural parameters and functional information of the attacked model are modeled and dissected within the S-F network analyzer. Bit attack results indicate that the attack thresholds for fully connected networks are similar, whereas convolutional neural networks can vary by up to 100-fold. S-F network experimental results reveal that bit attacks disrupt the trained narrow distribution of structural parameters, forcing them towards uniformly, and the performance degradation is caused by reducing the global efficiency and clustering coefficient of functional information.

articleTitle: Do Agents Behave Aligned with Human Instructions? - An Automated Assessment Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: The artificial intelligent agents have achieved remarkable success in multi-robot control, intelligent transportation, and competitive games, etc. Thorough testing for these agents is urgently needed to ensure its robustness in the face of constantly changing and unexpected scenarios. Existing methods mainly focus on the robustness testing to check whether these agents can cope with diverse scenarios. However, ensuring an agent can behave aligned with human instructions is also highly demanded, especially in competitive games. In these scenarios, the human commander might require the agent to behave in their desired manner in order to check whether a specific human instruction can win the game. Moreover, it is quite challenging to automatically assess whether an agent behave aligned with human instructions, considering the fact that the agents' low-level behaviors can hardly directly match with the high-level natural language described human instructions. To address this challenge, we propose an automatic assessment approach ABIM for determining whether the agents behave aligned with human instructions based on LLM inference. Its general idea is to automatically transfer the agent behavior and human instructions into a unified description of the micro operation topological representation with the LLM's natural language understanding and inference capability. We conduct experiments with five human instructions on SMAC environment, and results show that we can make the assessment with Precision of 0.5775 to 0.8571 and Recall of 0.6087 to 1.0. This automatic assessment technology can facilitate the alignment testing of agents, therefore enhance their quality more comprehensively.

articleTitle: Enhancing Incremental Dataflow Analysis in an IDE
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Incremental dataflow analysis is a conventional technique adopted in syntax-directed editors, popularly used in Integrated Development Environments (IDEs). However, dataflow anomaly detection during program editing in IDEs remains a challenge due to the interaction with newer functionalities, such as AI-powered plugins like Copilot, which might insert and modify code lines directly. These interactions impact both the efficiency and effectiveness of dataflow anomaly detection processes. This paper introduces an enhanced incremental dataflow analysis approach in IDEs, focused on the analysis of dataflow within program structures. Our approach introduces a modified version of SP-tree, named SP-graph. This modification, involving the addition of supporting edges, facilitates data storage and enhances dataflow analysis incrementally. We also present a mechanism that streamlines dataflow anomaly detection within IDEs by identifying modifications that may impact dataflow, updating relevant data, and conducting immediate analysis. In addition, incremental concurrent anomaly detection in SP-graph shall be studied further. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through a case study.

articleTitle: Behavioral System Using SVM and CNN for Karate Injury Detection and Rehabilitation Process
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: The frequency of sports injuries is rising, and wounds to elite players are having a negatively impacted effect on the playing field. It's becoming more and more popular to prevent sports injuries. Several approaches have been employed in a range of sports wounds fields due to the development of machine learning. Using mixed models that blend supervised and unsupervised learning, this paper addresses the issue of karate injury treatment, rehabilitation, and prevention by presenting a novel behavioral technique to identify injuries and the recovery process in karate. In this case, supervised learning was done with SVM and CNN models, and unsupervised learning was done with an autoencoder. The analysis conducted through experimentation shows that The proposed framework can yield accurate outcomes. In actuality, Our model's accuracy for SVM and CNN is 99.58% and 99.66%, respectively. Keywords-SVM;Machine Learning; Injury sports; Unsupervised learning; Supervised learning; CNN.

articleTitle: A SSCPS safety assessment method based on mission risk
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Cyber physical system (CPS) is a complex system that deeply integrates computing, network communication and control equipment. It has broad application prospects in aerospace, industrial production, transportation and other fields, and it also faces very severe security challenges. Especially for some safety-critical CPS (SSCPS), security issues will have serious consequences. How to carry out security assessment for safety-critical CPS systems has always been a hot issue in CPS research. This paper proposes a task risk-based SSCPS security assessment method. By decomposing the key tasks of the SSCPS system, identifying system risk elements based on task characteristics, and establishing the impact relationship between tasks and risk factors such as assets, vulnerabilities, and threats, construct a security assessment index system based on mission risk, and propose a security fusion method to achieve multilevel and multidimensional security assessment of SSCPS.

articleTitle: Bit Attacking Deep Neural Networks Based on Complex Networks Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: With the widespread application of deep learning technology in safety-critical systems, the issues of security and robustness are increasingly prominent, becoming an important topic that cannot be ignored. In addition to input-side threats represented by adversarial examples, model-side attacks such as poisoning attacks or bit flipping have also become fatal security threats in deep learning systems. Despite existing research in bit-flip attack being able to achieve significant attack effects by flipping a small number of bits, there still lacks effective bit attack strategies in dealing with limitations such as the lack of specific use cases, inability to perform forward propagation, and the presence of gradient masking. Therefore, this paper proposes a bit attack strategy based on complex network theory for fully connected neural networks (FCNNs). This strategy relies solely on the structural information of the model, abstracting the neural network into a directed weighted graph, and creating graph structural metrics of the neural network. Utilizing these metrics to identify vulnerable neurons and weights, it guides the execution of bit attacks. Experimental results demonstrate that bit attacks guided by complex network metrics are significantly superior to random attacks, and attacks guided by Link Weights metrics require only up to 50 bits at most to increase the neural network error by 80%.

articleTitle: Research of Military Cyber Operation Forensic and Analysis in Russia-Ukraine Conflict
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: The Russia-Ukraine conflict represents the first regional military confrontation between major (and external) powers that is thoroughly interspersed with cyber operations throughout the main military theater. In essence, the conflict has served as a testing ground for examining the impact of cyber actions on military operations, with its characteristics in cyber forensics and analysis yet to be fully explored. Firstly, this paper delves into the cyber operations and typical military cyber actions observed in the Russia-Ukraine conflict. Secondly, drawing upon the report issued by the Ukrainian National Security Service titled “Cyber Operation Of Russian Intelligence Services As A Component Of Confrontation On The Battlefield,” this paper conduct a study on the forensic investigation and analysis of these typical military cyber actions. Lastly, this paper summarizes the characteristics of military cyber actions and their forensic analysis in the Russia-Ukraine conflict, highlighting the challenges faced in cyber forensics in a real-world war scenario.

articleTitle: Detecting Bias in LLMs' Natural Language Inference Using Metamorphic Testing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: The increasing integration of Large Language Mod-els (LLMs) into pivotal decision-making contexts highlights the necessity for rigorous scrutiny to ensure fairness, especially in tasks involving Natural Language Processing (NLP). This paper introduces a novel method employing Metamorphic Testing (MT) to discern bias within the Natural Language Inference (NLI) task performed by LLMs. Our approach establishes a structured framework for generating test cases using Metamorphic Relations (MRs), incorporating nuanced demographic attributes such as sex, race, occupation, age, and socioeconomic status into textual inputs. We conduct prelimi-nary experiment with 3 common datasets, over 400k test cases in 4 state-of-art LLMs. Through evaluation of model predictions across these MRs, we unveil potential biases indicative of fairness violations. Preliminary investigations conducted with prominent LLMs underscore the effectiveness of our method in illuminating disparities in model performance, thus providing valuable insights into the bias implications of LLMs in NLI tasks. Our method is intuitive and adaptable for other NLP tasks. To the best of our knowledge, this represents the first application of MT to NLI bias detection.

articleTitle: Enhancing Software Security Analysis: Targeted Test Case Generation through Constraint Solving in Interactive Application Security Testing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Interactive Application Security Testing (IAST) is an innovative approach to improving software security assessment by combining the strengths of static and dynamic analysis, offering a more comprehensive and accurate assessment. This hybrid approach enables the identification of true positives resulting from static analysis, via confirmation through dynamic analysis. This paper presents techniques for generating specific test cases to verify static analysis findings by employing constraint-solving. Given the necessity for enhanced efficiency and accuracy in vulnerability identification in resource-constrained environments, such as embedded systems, where memory management issues are a significant vulnerability, our solution will concentrate on C code applications. Accordingly, one particular challenge that will be addressed is how to deal with pointers and memory management during the constraints collection. Furthermore, we will introduce methods that are used to handle external function calls - which pose a particular challenge because their source code is usually not available - and to cope with the state explosion problem through the early detection of paths that do not require further exploration.

articleTitle: Secure OTA Software Updates for Connected Vehicles Using LoRaWAN and Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Over-the-Air (OTA) software updates are becoming essential for connected vehicles, allowing remote updates that eliminate the need for physical access to each vehicle. This significantly reduces downtime and operational costs while keeping vehicular software up-to-date against emerging threats and technological advancements. However, this conventional approach is susceptible to various challenges, including security vulnerabilities, limited connections, and potential network unreliability, which may impede the effective deployment of updates. To address these issues, we investigate the integration of LoRaWAN with blockchain technology and the InterPlanetary File System (IPFS) for the connected vehicles. LoRaWAN offers long-range communication with end-to-end encryption, while blockchain provides transparency and IPFS offers efficient’ distributed storage. This dual-layered security approach also benefits from LoRaWAN's coverage and low power usage, and blockchain's tamper-proof nature. Furthermore, this paper assesses the feasibility of LoRaWAN through simulations, to determine the ideal conditions for effective OTA execution utilizing LoRaWAN technology in the connected vehicles. Our findings indicate that this approach is viable for updates targeting performance enhancements and a wide range of applications.

articleTitle: Topology Design of Electronic and Electrical Architecture for Time-Sensitive Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: The vehicle's Electrical/Electronic Architecture (EEA) serves as the foundation for implementing various functions of intelligent vehicles. This paper analyzes and summarizes the layout of the distributed vehicle EEA and discusses the advantages of Time-Sensitive Network (TSN) in the field of in-vehicle communications. Building upon the analysis, this paper combines the advantages of function-oriented and zone-oriented EEA and proposes a function-zone EEA for TSN. Four EEA network topology forms are evaluated based on communication delay, network load, cost and flexibility. Based on the OMNET++ framework, this paper conducts simulation verification of autonomous driving and body control data flows. The results show that the ring and mesh network topology can significantly reduce communication delays, enabling high-speed and scalable transmission for invehicle communication.

articleTitle: Recursive Generation of Multi-Qubits Control Gate to Facilitate the Grover's Quantum Algorithm in Large Scale Database Search
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Context: Grover's algorithm is a powerful tool in the realm of quantum computing because it offers exponential speedup over classical linear searching for unstructured / unsorted search problems. However, it is challenging to construct efficient and scalable circuits for a multi-input control gate in the algorithm, particularly with a huge number of qubit inputs. Problem: Traditional circuit construction methods often require manual composition for the multi-input gate from basic quantum gates, which can be time consuming and error prone, thus hindering practical implementation. Moreover, the number of simple gates in the composition grows exponentially with the addition of each qubit. Method: This research provides an approach to recursively generate the oracle using Toffoli gates as the fundamental units to enhance scalability and reusability while maintaining effectiveness. The methodology leverages IBM Qiskit and Quantum Lab to simulate quantum computation to prove the practicality and feasibility. Result: The findings from the experiments between recursively and non-recursively generated circuits suggest that our recursive approach can offer comparable accuracy and computational complexity compared to the non-recursive approach. However, it tends to require a larger number of basic quantum gates due to a lack of circuit optimization. Conclusion: The results showcase the applicability of utilizing recursion as a speedy and economical alternative to generate circuits when implementing the Grover's algorithm. It not only presents potential scalability benefits, but also creates an avenue for further research on test verification and performance improvement to the computing community when running in actual quantum hardware.

articleTitle: The Interweaving of Institutional Investors, Cloud Computing Technology and Sustainable Growth of Tourism Enterprises
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Cloud computing technology is a modern computing method and service model based on the Internet. This paper utilizes Python software and machine learning to extract annual reports of listed tourism companies. Subsequently, it conducts word frequency statistics on keywords associated with cloud computing technology to evaluate the adoption level of cloud computing technology in tourism enterprises. Subsequently, using STATA 16.0, this paper analyzes 1500 Chinese tourism-related listed enterprises from 2007 to 2022. It empirically tests the influence mechanism of cloud computing technology on the sustainable development of tourism enterprises. The research findings show that cloud computing technology has a positive impact on the sustainable development of tourism enterprises. After a series of tests, it has been proven that these results are robust. This study extends the research on the factors promoting the adoption of cloud computing technology to promote sustainable development. It emphasizes the importance of integrating cloud computing technology into the sustainable development strategy of tourism enterprises and highlights the moderating role of institutional investors' shareholding ratio. It offers practical recommendations for tourism businesses to efficiently manage data, evaluate risks, and maximize resources through the use of cloud computing technology. Currently, the adoption rate of cloud computing technology by Chinese tourism enterprises is relatively low, and the application level varies greatly. Institutional investors can play a role in supporting sustainable development. However, excessively concentrated holdings may pose potential risks, ultimately undermining the decision-making rights of other shareholders and negatively impacting the business. This study focuses on listed companies in a specific tourism-related industry. Future research will broaden the scope of analysis to encompass more industries and utilize various data analysis methods to achieve a more comprehensive understanding of the relationship between cloud computing, institutional investors, and corporate sustainability.

articleTitle: Efficient Detection of Selfish Mining Attacks on Large-Scale Blockchain Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Selfish mining attacks pose a significant and ongoing security threat to blockchain networks, including major platforms like Bitcoin and Ethereum. Understanding and effectively countering these attacks is crucial for maintaining the stability and integrity of these networks. This attack strategy involves a miner or a group of miners seeking to gain an advantage by delaying the immediate broadcasting of their mined blocks to the network. The selfish miners potentially mine more blocks in secret, increasing their rewards at the expense of other miners and the stability of the blockchain. Research has mainly focused on detecting this attack by analyzing data related to blocks and forks. This paper presents a new approach to efficiently detect selfish mining attacks in large-scale networks by analyzing various network indicators. To achieve this, we simulate a Bitcoin network and generate a dataset consisting of several features of individual miners and the overall network. We select the most reliable indicators by analyzing network features and reducing feature dimensions. Then, we employ random forest classification (RFC) to classify benign and selfish network behaviors. This approach not only achieves enhanced accuracy (99.96%), surpassing state-of-the-art methods utilizing deep learning, but also significantly reduces computational, storage, and temporal complexities. In doing so, it fortifies blockchain security more efficiently and accurately.

articleTitle: SIS: A Syntactic Information-based Span-level Model for Aspect Sentiment Triplets Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Aspect Sentiment Triplet Extraction (ASTE) is a critical sub-task within aspect-based sentiment analysis (ABSA), focusing on identifying triplets consisting of aspect terms, opinion terms, and their corresponding sentiments. Current predominant ASTE methodologies can be categorized as token-level and span-level approaches. Token-level methods heavily rely on the interactions between individual tokens representing aspect and opinion terms, which may not effectively handle aspect and opinion terms composed of multiple words, thereby impacting their performance. Conversely, span-level methods consider multiple words as a single span when predicting triplets, thus maintaining the relationship between words more effectively than token-level methods. However, the span-level also encounters challenges, such as enumerating spans solely based on word positions in a sentence overlooks the syntactic relationships between words, and exhaustively enumerating all spans results in significant computational overhead. To solve them, we propose a syntactic information-based span-level model (SIS). The model acquires syntactic information and employs a graph convolutional neural network (GCN) to extract syntactic dependency features. Furthermore, we introduce a part-of-speech (POS)-based technique for span trimming to remove invalid spans. The experimental findings indicate that we achieved the highest F1-scores of 64.40%, 71.14%, and 72.26% on Lap14, Res15, and Res16, and the highest precision of 79.51% on Res14 among four benchmark datasets.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Interest-Aware Message-Passing GCN for Recommendation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Over the past few years, Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN) have emerged as a promising tool in the field of recommendation. They have the ability to effectively learn user and item embeddings by leveraging collaborative signals from higher-order neighbors. Nevertheless, the recommendation models based on GCN also face a common issue. As more layers are added, the node embeddings start to become increasingly similar and eventually become indistin-guishable, leading to a decline in performance. To address the issues at hand, we present a recommendation model called DIMP-GCN. This model utilizes a Dynamic Interest-aware Message-Passing approach, where users and interacted items are organized into distinct subgraphs based on their interests. Within each subgraph, single-layer graph convolution operations are performed. As a result, the users who have been updated are divided based on their interests once again, leading to dynamic changes in subgraph partitioning as the network layers stack. Nodes are able to acquire more accurate representations through this process. We conduct extensive experiments on three established datasets, showcasing the superior performance of our DIMP-GCN compared to other state-of-the-art GCN-based recommendation models.

articleTitle: A Reliability Benchmarking Method for Linux
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: The main challenges faced in conducting reliability assessment of highly reliable computer products by using traditional methods are high cost, long cycle, and low au-tomation level. Although the reliability model based on small samples can acquire reliability attributes, the time expenditure remains significant. The accelerated life testing method is still in the exploratory stage due to the complexity of failure mechanisms in highly reliable computer products. This paper presents an implementation scheme of dependability bench-marking for reliability assessment of Linux operating system. The benchmarking results obtained can be used to compare the differences in reliability of different Linux distributions. The occurrence process of Linux kernel faults is modeled as Poisson process, and the timing of fault injection is determined according to the rule of exponential distribution of fault occurrence interval. The faults composing the fault injection sequence are derived from a validated fault mode library, in which the proportion of the number of fault modes of different kernel functional modules is used to characterize the spatial distribution of faults in actual situations. The selected stable operating phase software reliability model is an exponentially distributed homogeneous Poisson process model. It can produce reference values for the main reliability attributes of Linux, such as failure rate, Mean Time to Failure (MTTF), and reliability function. We also develop a tool prototype based on the proposed implementation scheme and use it for reliability assessment of CentOS Stream 8, AnolisOS-8.4-GA, openSUSE 15.3, Ubuntu 20.04.3, Fedora 35 and openEuler-20.03-LTS-SP3 Linux distributions released during the same period.

articleTitle: A Fuzzing Method for Embedded Bus Based on Dynamic Mutation of Message Sequences
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: As an important support for the communication link of embedded systems, the bus protocol faces many security threats while meeting diverse business needs, and how to ensure the security of the bus link of embedded systems has become an important security issue. In order to meet the requirements of generalized security detection of embedded system bus protocols, this paper proposes a fuzzing method for embedded bus protocol based on dynamic mutation of message sequences. Based on the bus protocol specification, we model the protocol message and interaction process, and realize the fuzzing test of the protocol process in combination with the association of messages in the message sequence. At the same time, we combined the fuzzer with a timer to increase the time perception of the method. In order to verify the effectiveness of our method, this paper applies the proposed method to the CAN bus fuzzing of the Internet of Vehicles simulation platform, and successfully finds a security flaw in the process of motor speed data frame processing of the platform. Moreover, we carry out a comparative experiment with several common fuzzing tools, and the experimental results show that in the defect detection of the CAN bus of the Internet of Vehicles simulation platform, our method can increase the automatic mutation support for the interval_time field, and can discover more security defects.

articleTitle: Immersive Traffic Interactive Simulator for Multi-Agent
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
