abstract: Interaction in complex traffic scenarios poses significant risks, but existing research lacks a thorough analysis of interaction mechanisms. This gap presents challenges for self-driving cars to navigate such complex scenarios safely. Mining interaction mechanisms heavily rely on real-world data, which is costly and risky. Therefore, interaction data acquisition often occurs through simulation test environments. However, current driving scene simulators typically use predefined rules to simulate interactions, failing to represent genuine responses in real scenarios accurately. This study proposes an immersive interaction simulator system for multiple agents to address this limitation and obtain authentic interaction data within simulations. The simulator covers five common interaction cases in traffic scenarios, and three interaction types: vehicle-vehicle, human-vehicle, and pedestrian-vehicle-vehicle interactions. Vehicle interaction data is incorporated using driving simulator devices, while pedestrian interaction data is captured through virtual reality (VR) and motion capture devices. Real-time closed-loop feedback of simulated interactions is ensured by implementing a multi-computer communication protocol. Furthermore, the system includes a comprehensive data recording module, enabling playback analysis and rewriting of interactive cases. The development of this interaction simulator holds promise for deepening our understanding of interaction mechanisms and has potential applications in autonomous driving, thereby enhancing the safety of self-driving cars.

articleTitle: Research on Parametric Generation of Automobile Styling Based on Grasshopper
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Automakers are launching new energy sub-brands for market distinction and premium positioning, facing design uniformity issues. Although underutilized in the industry, parametric design's potential for form innovation suggests a transformative impact on car design. This research is based on the theory of abstract forms in automotive styling, analyzing the shape rules and application methods of abstract forms. A form generation model based on random lines has been established in Grasshopper, and the application process of this parametric generation technology has been fully constructed in conjunction with actual design cases. The model produces a variety of stochastic forms, which are selected and optimized according to the characteristics of the vehicle type and aesthetic principles to obtain an abstract prototype. This abstract prototype is gradually evolved into a core abstract form, a sub-vehicle form, and a vehicle form through Rhino software, and a NURBS model is constructed based on the vehicle form. This paper innovatively constructs a car styling design method based on parametric generation, namely ‘Parametric Design - Stochastic Form - Abstract Prototype - Core Abstract Form - Sub-vehicle Form - Vehicle Form - Production Car Style’, and applies it to specific design cases, verifying the feasibility of this technical route.

articleTitle: Immersing and Perceiving in Tourism Scenarios: The Interaction Mechanism between Digital Technologies and Tourists
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: This study explores the impact of digital technologies on immersive tourism experiences, focusing on the interaction mechanisms between these technologies and tourists. With the rise of VR, AR, mobile apps, and wearables, digital tools have become pivotal in enhancing tourist engagement and satisfaction. The main contribution of this research is the development of a systematic framework for constructing immersive tourism experiences. This framework involves collecting and analysing tourism resource data, selecting appropriate technologies, and generating interaction mechanisms. Additionally, a comprehensive case study categorises tourism resources into cognitive, emotional, aesthetic, and intelligent interactions, and validates the framework through statistical analysis. The findings reveal that these interactions significantly contribute to creating high-quality immersive experiences. Recommendations for integrating digital technologies into tourism are provided to enrich tourist experiences and foster deeper connections with destinations. This research offers valuable insights into the effective utilisation of digital tools in tourism, paving the way for innovative and captivating tourist engagements.

articleTitle: The Application of LLMs in the Analysis and Modeling of Software Requirements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: In modern software engineering, requirements analysis and modeling are key steps in requirements engineering, influencing the subsequent system design and implementation. Traditional requirements analysis and modeling methods usually involve multiple stakeholders such as requirements providers and analysts working together collaboratively and iteratively, requiring a significant amount of manpower. It is of great significance to reduce the burden on requirements providers and analysts and improve the efficiency of analysis and modeling. In existing work, some merely utilize knowledge repositories to provide more knowledge in support of analysis or modeling, while others employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques to automate the analysis or modeling process. However, neither has relieved the burden on requirements providers and analysts. The emergence of large language models(LLMs) has brought new possibilities to requirements analysis and modeling. LLMs can combine knowledge base processing and understanding of large amounts of natural language data, providing a new automated requirement analysis method. This paper proposes an automated requirements analysis and modeling method for Support Vector Machine(SVM) classifier and LLMs - SVM-LLMs. The method is deployed based on the intelligent requirement service platform - “Wisdom Requirement Communication”, which combines SVM and LLMs to effectively improve the accuracy of requirements analysis and significantly reduce the time in the software development process.

articleTitle: Exploring the Efficacy of Dynamic Approaches in Database Encryption and Translational Security
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: In current information security management, many security protection standards based on network security have been established. Based on communication security, we will develop secure channels and data transmission rules to reduce the possibility of disclosure in data collection. This method is sufficient to meet the needs of all parties regarding the security maintenance services required for communication security. However, due to the software system development week, there are concerns about information security due to possible code vulnerabilities that may arise during software development. This study is based on the encryption design for secure maintenance and operation of the database and uses an intermediary system to encrypt data fields. In the study, a single encryption key design is designed for each data field, and an agent call for the data form encrypts each column. From different key data encryption operation ensures that the data has independent encryption operation procedures, which reduces the possibility of leaking a large amount of plaintext data when the database is attacked. In this study, an intermediate conversion encryption engine is constructed to automatically generate a set of independent security keys before each row of data is written to the database. At the same time, before each piece of data is written into the database, there is an independent key for the field information that lets encryption and decryption be performed. In our experiment result, we found that since each piece of data is encrypted by its independent writing method, it can be used to improve and solve the problem of data leakage caused by SQL injection into the database by SQL query, and at the same time, more strengthened the security technical difficulties of traditional data masking.

articleTitle: Analysis of Reliable Architecture Techniques for Adaptive Adversarial Systems of System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Driven by new technological innovations, Adaptive Adversarial Systems of Systems (AASS) are rapidly developing, and their reliability issues are increasingly receiving widespread attention. This architecture efficiently integrates heterogeneous combat resources from different fields to achieve rapid fusion and collaboration of multi-source information, ensuring its ability to continuously, accurately, and stably execute predetermined tasks in complex, high-pressure, and adversarial environments. However, how to design and implement an efficient, reliable, adaptive, and adversarial system architecture still faces many challenges. This paper aims to delve into the design principles and key technologies of the architecture of AASS. Finally, AASS and its future development trends and challenges are proposed, and a brief summary of AASS reliability architecture is provided.

articleTitle: YOLO-TSD: A Recognition and Detection Method for Traffic Sign Based on YOLOv5
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: In the realm of self-driving technology and vehicular security, the identification of traffic signs is of paramount importance. To address the challenges encountered in the detection process, such as insufficient effective features of traffic signs and complex background environment. Within this article, a novel optimization technique referred to as YOLO-TSD, which stands for a recognition and detection method for traffic signs employing YOLOv5, is presented. This approach incorporates an EVCBlock module as well as the EIOU loss function to augment the precision and constancy in bounding box regression. Initially, the integration of the EVCBlock into YOLOv5's fundamental network structure occurs to bolster pertinent features through the amalgamation of both comprehensive and detailed data. Then, we use EIOU loss function to accelerate the matching process between target boxes and anchor boxes. Ultimately, the developed algorithm is employed to identify the location of road signs within the photograph. The experimental results show that the MAP of YOLO-TSD on the TT100K training set has experienced a 4.91% enhancement when compared to the initial YOLOv5, and the model boasts robust stability that aids in the detection of traffic signals.

articleTitle: Incarnation-Mediated: Cognitive Measurement of Virtual Scenes and Analysis of Complex Active Adaptive Behaviors in Realistic Scenography
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: In the field of cave fresco research, this study aims to address the degradation of frescoes caused by natural erosion and human damage. In order to improve the science and effectiveness of the restoration work, we propose an innovative restoration method that combines eye-tracking technology and an “avatar” generation model. By carefully analyzing the visual attention of the observer, we identified visual hotspots in the murals and used them as the basis for restoration. Case studies have shown that this method can significantly improve the restoration results and has been recognized by experts and the public. This research result not only verifies the effectiveness of the proposed method, but also provides a new paradigm for the future restoration of cave wall paintings, which has wide potential for popularization and application.

articleTitle: MTPI: Multimodal Trajectory Prediction for Autonomous Driving via Informer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: The multimodal prediction of surrounding vehicle trajectories serves as a valuable tool in assisting autonomous vehicles in making safe and rational decisions. The complexity and partial observability of autonomous driving scenarios result in the generation of dense data between target vehicles and moving entities as well as traffic scenes, which includes static data such as the number of lanes and dynamic data with timing information. Due to the impact of dense data on the accuracy of trajectory prediction, it becomes crucial to model different sets of input features. Modeling different input feature sets can provide a more comprehensive and accurate representation of the data and ultimately improve the accuracy of trajectory prediction. In this paper, we propose a multimodal trajectory prediction method for autonomous driving based on Informer, called MTPI. The MTPI model uses an encoder-decoder structure based on Informer for multimodal trajectory prediction. The proposed model enhances trajectory prediction accuracy by modeling various input feature sets, enabling a better understanding and capturing of the relationship between the target vehicle, moving entities, and the traffic scene. To optimize internal memory utilization and reduce computational complexity, we incorporate self-attention distilling and probsparse self-attention operations based on Informer into the model. Experimental results on the Argoverse dataset demonstrate that MTPI achieves outstanding performance in multimodal trajectory prediction.

articleTitle: Explainable AI Applied in Healthcare: A Case Study of Diabetes Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: As the diabetic population grows, digital technology offers new possibilities for disease management. Explainable AI (XAI) can analyze data such as blood glucose, BMI, and genetics, providing transparent explanations for diabetes prediction models, thus enhancing trust among healthcare professionals. This study applies the SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) method to a gradient boosting decision tree model for diabetes prediction. With ten-fold cross-validation, the model shows excellent accuracy, precision, recall, Fl score, and AUC value. Using SHAP, blood glucose, BMI, and age were identified as key predictive features, aligning with clinical knowledge. The analysis also shows a positive correlation between these features and model output, with blood pressure and pregnancy history demonstrating nonlinear effects. The findings suggest that SHAP explanations improve the model's explainability and credibility, supporting personalized treatment.

articleTitle: A-TCN: Attention-Based TCN for OSS Reliability Prediction on High-Dimensional Fault Dataset
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Open source software (OSS) has been widely applied in various fields, and its reliability evaluation and prediction have become a research focus. Unlike the traditional development paradigm of closed-source software, OSS allows users to freely study, modify, copy, and distribute their code, thereby generating more fault information. These pieces of information will be meticulously recorded in the bug tracking systems, providing a rich foundation for predicting the reliability of OSS. Meanwhile, deep learning methods have been widely used in OSS reliability prediction due to their excellent learning ability and model construction ability. However, existing deep learning based OSS reliability prediction models still face many challenges, such as insufficient fault information in the dataset leading to limited model performance, the recurrent structure of most deep learning models resulting in vanishing gradients, exploding gradients, and insufficient training efficiency. In this paper, we utilize the fault data recorded in the bug tracking system to construct a high-dimensional feature (HDF) dataset by mapping feature values to numerical values. This enables the model to accurately understand the sequential relationships between different features, while avoiding dimension expansion and increased computational complexity. Then, we employ the so-called HDF selection (HDFS) method to select feature subsets and generate a high-dimensional fault dataset. Moreover, we integrate the Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) attention mechanism into the Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN) framework and propose the Attention-based TCN (A-TCN) model. Finally, we validate the effectiveness of the model through an actual OSS based on two real fault datasets. The experimental results show that the A-TCN model outperforms other deep learning models, including Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Gated Recurrent Units (GRU), and TCN.

articleTitle: Wuli-Shili-Renli-Jili System Approach and Its Application in Large Model Value Alignment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: As artificial intelligence systems enter a rapid development phase, large models, serving as a new type of hybrid intelligence system for human-machine collaboration, still lack a system methodology that suits them. This study extends the Wuli-Shili-Renli (WSR) system approach, innovatively proposing a Wuli- Shili- Renli- Jili (WSRJ) system approach suitable for large models. It constructs the connotation of the Jili element and explores the application of WSRJ system approach in the technology research of large model value alignment, providing a multi-dimensional system analysis framework of function, logic, humanity, and technology.

articleTitle: An Approach to Optimize Symbolic Execution in Ethereum Smart Contracts
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: As the application of smart contracts in blockchain technology becomes increasingly widespread, their security issues have emerged as a focal point of both research and practice. Although symbolic execution technology has been extensively applied for the detection of security vulnerabilities in smart contracts, its limitations in terms of execution efficiency and code coverage remain significant. In response to these challenges, this study introduces an innovative method named HoneyToken-DetectorRev, which optimizes traditional symbolic execution through program slicing technology, aiming to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of smart contract security detection. By selecting ten smart contracts from the Ethereum platform, which vary in business logic and complexity, we conducted an empirical analysis of HoneyToken-DetectorRev. The experimental results demonstrate that this method significantly improves the efficiency of smart contract detection without sacrificing precision. This research not only provides an effective technical approach for the security detection of smart contracts but also offers theoretical and practical guidance for further enhancing the security of blockchain applications.

articleTitle: Research on the Construction Method of Multimodal Dataset for Hazardous Chemicals Warehouse Applied to Inspection Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: The safety distance detection in hazardous chemical warehouses based on automatic inspection vehicles is a very promising technical solution. High quality datasets are essential for developing reliable autonomous driving algorithms, but there is a significant shortage of such data. This paper uses a low-cost, easily deployable monocular camera and incorporates a pose expansion algorithm for synthetic viewpoint rendering within Neural Radiance Fields to expand RGB images. Using structured light technology to generate depth images, the RGB image and depth image are calculated by depth backprojection formula to obtain three-dimensional point cloud. Combined with environmental parameters and relevant standards and regulations, a multimodal dataset for hazardous chemicals warehouses is constructed. The quality of the dataset is assessed using multiple indicators. Experimental results show that this generation framework is effective and the dataset is comprehensive and accurate, providing valuable insights and research for constructing new datasets in related fields.

articleTitle: FedCST: Federated Learning on Heterogeneous Resource-constrained Devices Using Clustering and Split Training
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: With the rapid development of 5G and Internet of Things (IoT) technologies, edge devices such as sensors, smartphones, and wearable devices have become increasingly prevalent. The massive amount of distributed data generated by these devices offers unprecedented opportunities for deep learning, especially in fields like computer vision and edge computing. However, this data often exists in isolated data silos, and due to its privacy-sensitive nature, it cannot be directly processed in a centralized manner. Additionally, the data heterogeneity and devices heterogeneity further exacer-bates the challenges in federated learning (FL). Moreover, with the implementation of data privacy protection regulations, user demand for privacy protection is growing significantly. Therefore, how to effectively utilize dispersed data for distributed collaborative learning while ensuring data privacy is a pressing issue that needs to be addressed in the field of FL. In response to these challenges, this work has conducted research on clustering and segmentation FL algorithms for heterogeneous resource-constrained devices. A lightweight homogeneous device clustering strategy has been designed, which incorporates a split learning (SL) mechanism to enhance the accuracy and training efficiency of FL models. This approach reduces the load on resource-constrained devices and improves privacy security. Consequently, this method can meet the dual requirements of privacy protection and computational efficiency in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: High Accurate, Low Latency Conversion of Spiking Neural Networks with BLIF Neurons
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs), acknowledged as the third generation of neural network technology, stand out for their efficiency and closer resemblance to biological brain functions compared to traditional Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs). However, training SNNs can be challenging because it's difficult to differentiate between spike trains. Converting ANNs to SNNs has emerged as a promising solution to this issue. Yet, ANN-SNN conversion has its limitations: it cannot represent negative spikes as captured by Dynamic Vision Sensors (DVS) cameras and suffers from severe accuracy loss with short simulation time-steps. In this paper, by developed a bi-threshold dynamic mechanism, we proposed the Bi-threshold Linear Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (BLIF) neu-ron, relieving constraints on the negative spike expression of SNNs. Secondly, we analyzed the residual error between BLIF neuron and Leaky ReL U activation function, and proposed a Stepwise Leaky ReLU activation function more suitable for BLIF neuron under membrane potential encoding, which ensures zero residual error in the ANN-SNN conversion, even with very short simulation time-steps. Last, we developed a zonal convergence testing method to eliminate the distribution error in the ANN-SNN conversion. These three approaches help us convert the ANNs to SNNs with no distribution error and residual error, which have high accuracy, low latency and good robustness, and have achieved the state-of-the-art performance on various datasets such as CIFAR10, CIFAR100 and ImageNet.

Author Keywords: artificial neural network (ANN)-to-spiking neural network (SNN) conversion

articleTitle: Directed Fuzzing with Adaptive Path Guidance and Weighted Distribution
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Existing directed fuzzing tool AFLGO calculates the distance to the target locations using a shortest path first approach to prioritize test cases. This results in potential paths to the target location that might not be executed. Moreover, the scoring strategy in AFLGO is calculated using fixed weights, which does not fully leverage the data and feedback generated during the testing process. In this paper, we propose a new guiding mechanism that marks key locations on reachable paths to the target locations. During execution, the priority of test cases is dynamically adjusted based on the coverage of these reachable paths to guide the generation of test cases. Additionally, we designed an adaptive weight distribution algorithm that continuously adjusts the weights of various influencing factors for test cases, allowing for more reasonable mutation time allocations in subsequent tests. We implemented these strategies and conducted experiments on four different open-source test programs. The experimental results show that our proposed method has significant improvements in code coverage and vulnerability detection compared to AFLGO.

articleTitle: The Effect of Variable Strength Combinatorial Coverage for Neurons on Fault Detection in Deep Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: In order to evaluate whether a test set for deep neural networks (DNNs) is adequate, people proposed many test adequacy metrics for DNNs testing. As an enhancement of the classic fixed strength combinatorial testing technique, variable strength combinatorial testing has also been used for white-box testing of DNNs to evaluate whether the activation behavior of neurons is diverse during test execution. However, it is still inconclusive whether the variable strength combi-natorial coverage of neurons is beneficial to the testing of DNNs. We conduct an empirical study in this paper to answer how the variable strength combinatorial coverage of neurons affects the fault detection in DNNs. The experimental results show a medium or strong negative correlation between the variable strength combinatorial coverage of neurons and the number of adversarial examples for DNNs. This may imply that adversarial examples generated using the same adversarial attack method have similarity in the characteristics of neural output.

articleTitle: Enhancing Programming Competition Performance: A Data-Driven Approach to Personalized Training
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: In programming competition training, the key to boosting students' competitiveness and award chances is to provide personalized problem recommendations based on their coding skills. Traditional uniform training problems fail to account for the individual differences among students, and cannot guarantee a perfect alignment between problems and students' abilities. Each student possesses a unique learning pace, comprehension level, and mastery degree, making a standardized method likely to overlook or excessively chal-lenge certain students. This impacts their learning effective-ness and enthusiasm. The personalized and flexible problems recommendation algorithm is urgently needed. We propose four novel problem recommendation algorithms, which aim to facilitate the personalized generation of problem sets tailored to students' skill levels. Specifically, we use programming history records to evaluate students' strengths and weaknesses, to recommend suitable exercises and adjust recommendation algorithms based on their performance in these programming problems. In a case study at Beijing University of Chemical Technology (BUCT), the implementation of these personalized training algorithms leads to a 33% improvement in final performance compared to traditional approaches. This suggests a promising new direction for programming education.

articleTitle: Preset Emotional Experience: Adaptive Detection and Complexity Interpretation of Implicit Order in Facial Emotion Recognition Calculations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: This paper explores the phenomenon of religious instigation in cave statues and dynamic perceptual participation in the field of art and design. By applying the 4E cognitive theory, we study the role of embodiment, embedding, extension and activity in the perceptual process. With the help of artistic practice, we further explore the application of dynamic thinking in expression recognition algorithms and demonstrate the effectiveness and stability of the algorithms through case verification. The study found that perception is dynamic and unstable, limited by current cognition, and involves analysis of directional behavior and predictive levels. This study not only enriches the theoretical foundation of related fields, but also provides new ideas and directions for the future research on cave statues and the development of expression recognition technology.

articleTitle: Navigating the Risks: A Review of Safety Issues in Large Language Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Since the advent of Large Language Models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT, natural language processing has seen significant progress, providing timely, context-aware, and intelligent solutions across various domains. While users benefit greatly from these advancements, increasing safety concerns have surfaced, highlighting vulnerabilities and their impact on daily tasks. It is crucial to understand the implications of LLMs and not simply trust their outputs blindly. This paper reviews literature on LLM safety issues including data privacy, security, adversarial attacks, and compliance with laws and ethical guidelines.. Specifically, limitations, risks, testing methods, and evaluation criteria from a safety perspective are discussed. Based on these insights, it proposes suggestions to mitigate current safety challenges. The goal is to aid researchers and developers in designing safer, more reliable LLMs and to enhance user interactions with these technologies.

articleTitle: A Fuzzy AHP-based Quantitative Framework to Prioritize the Crowd-Based Requirements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Softwarerequirement plays a vital role in the success of a software project. However, the quality of requirement management remains a key challenge for a project manager, especially in a Crowdsourcing context. In Crowdsourcing, the customers belong from diverse locations; thereby, providing the redundant and inconsistent requirements for a targeted software system. To the best of our knowledge, the existing literature lacks in providing a quantitative framework that prioritizes the crucial factors affecting the requirement's management in the Crowdsourcing context. Motivated by this, we propose a quantitative framework that will be effective in ranking the Crowdsourcing-based requirements. For this purpose, the current study intends to identify various factors, that can affect the management of requirements, from the literature and also validates them from the practitioners. To accomplish this, we perform a systematic review and an empirical study. Moreover, we quantify the impact of each factor using the capability of a multi-criteria decision-making oriented Fuzzy- Analytical Hierarchy Process (F-AHP) technique. Subsequently, we also employ a multi-perspective prioritization technique to obtain the data from the relevant personnel to validate the quantified score. To assess the performance of the proposed quantitative framework, we considered a real-world Smart Home case study. Moreover, the efficacy of the adopted F-AHP technique is validated by comparing it with the traditional AHP technique. The results indicate that the F-AHP technique significantly outperformed the baseline technique.

articleTitle: Testing and Reinforcement Learning - A Structured Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Reinforcement Learning has gained much attention in the last decade, leading to substantial progress in Artificial Intelligence and its applications, especially in games and other areas where agents interact to learn and adapt to complex environments successfully. In this paper, we focus on reinforcement learning in the context of software and system testing. Specifically, we want to review the use of reinforcement learning in testing particularly test automation and testing approaches used for assuring the quality of reinforcement learning implementations. For this purpose, we carried out a structured literature review that considered Scopus, the digital libraries of IEEE and ACM. Using exclusion and inclusion criteria, we finally obtained 79 scientific articles. We categorized these articles according to various criteria, like the testing methods used or the application of testing, e.g., for obtaining security vulnerabilities, for automated game testing devoid of human competitive intelligence aid, for exploring GUI actions and states, etc. Hence, most papers focus on applying reinforcement learning for testing, but there is little work on testing implementations of reinforcement learning.

articleTitle: A Land-Based War-Gaming Simulation Method Based on Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: War-gaming simulation is an important means of assisting and simulating modern warfare, characterized by simulation, uncertainty, and asymmetric gameplay. With the development of deep reinforcement learning techniques, deep reinforcement learning methods can be used to generate combat strategies in war-gaming simulations. This paper ad-dresses the challenges of complex instructions, sparse re-wards, and collaborative multi-agent combat in land-based war-gaming simulations. We propose a situation extraction method based on feature concatenation, design task-specific reward functions, and utilize the Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (MAPPO) algorithm to train intelligent agents. The proposed method achieves a good win rate in land-based war-gaming simulation scenarios, which is more reliable than the baselines.

articleTitle: StasogFL: A Fault Localization Method Based on Statement Association Graph
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: In the realm of software development, Software Fault Localization (SFL) is critical for enhancing software quality and maintenance. Traditional methods like Spectrum-Based Fault Localization (SBFL) have been foundational but often fall short in handling the complexity and intricacies of modern software systems. This paper introduces a novel graph-based fault localization method, StasogFL, which leverages a statement association graph to capture the intricate relationships within software structures. By integrating control flows, data flows, and function calls into a comprehensive graph model, our approach significantly improves fault localization's precision and efficiency. The empirical results from applying StasogFL on large Java projects demonstrate substantial improvements over traditional SBFL methods and other graph-based approaches, particularly in terms of fault prediction accuracy and localization efficiency. This paper not only showcases the effectiveness of StasogFL but also paves the way for future research to further refine and expand its application across more varied software maintenance scenarios.

articleTitle: An IT Community Code Quality Ranking Model Based on Sentiment Analysis and Fuzzy Multi-Attribute Decision-Making
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: With the rapid development of IT technology, the IT community has accumulated a large number of code snippets, but the quality of these codes varies, which makes it inconvenient for users to find and use codes. If these codes can be ranked according to their quality to provide reference for users, it will greatly improve user experience. Existing methods use machine learning techniques to rank code quality, but the extraction of features often carries the author's patterned subj ective judgment, and the evaluation standard is relatively single, in order to solve this problem, this paper proposes an intuitionistic fuzzy multi-attribute decision-making method based on user comments for code quality evaluation, which is divided into two steps, one is to take aspect-oriented sentiment analysis based on BERT pre-training model on user comments to obtain the fuzzy decision matrix. analysis to get the fuzzy decision matrix. The second is to use the TOPSIS fuzzy multi-attribute decision-making model and give different weighting schemes according to the content of different comments, and finally arrive at the answer ranking of a specific question. This study is based on the CSDN technical Q&A(Question and Answer) community data for instantiation verification, and the results show that the use of fuzzy multi-attribute decision-making can better adapt to the problem of the level of the commenters and differences in opinions, and the different weighting scheme better adapts to the different needs of the users who ask questions.

articleTitle: Rapid Accuracy Loss Evaluation for Quantized Neural Networks Using Attention-Based Multifactor Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Neural network quantization, the process of converting floating-point models into low-bit-width integer models, has become a key technology for reducing the computational and storage costs of neural network models. However, quantization inevitably leads to a loss of accuracy, making it particularly important to assess this loss quickly and accurately. Rapid evaluation can significantly save time and resources, especially during the model development and deployment phases, and facilitates rapid model iteration and optimisation. However, quantization accuracy loss is influenced by multiple factors, often involving multimodal data, which are difficult to model and integrate effectively. This paper proposes a multifactor modeling method based on attention mechanisms, which aims to analyse and simulate the relationship between quantization factors and neural network performance, thereby providing a method to quickly and accurately assess post-training quantization accuracy loss. Experimental results show that this method can quickly predict the accuracy of different neural network models on various computational tasks without relying on extensive test data, with a prediction error of only about 2%, effectively supporting rapid model development and iterative optimization. Codes will be available on https://github.com/ycjcy/Accuracy-Loss-Evaluation.

articleTitle: A Human-Machine Intervention Model of Autonomous Driving Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: While autonomous driving has been widely applied, they can not be fully embraced by individual users and society until their safety issues are addressed. The operation of autonomous driving system depends not only on the machine system but also on the human driver. However, in the current reliability assessment of human-machine system, human and machine are often regarded as functional units, neglecting the intervention process of human driver, resulting in underestimated reliability of autonomous driving vehicle. Consequently, in this paper, a human-machine intervention model of autonomous driving vehicle is proposed. In this model, the human driver can have more opportunities to intervene the vehicle than taking human driver and machine as functional units, yielding higher reliability of autonomous driving vehicle.

articleTitle: Heuristics for Strongly Killing Mutants in Software Mutation Testing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Software mutation testing helps a tester create test cases and improve the quality of a test set. In mutation testing, the original source code of a program is mutated by the tester and the resulting program is called a “mutant”. Testers design test cases to be able to distinguish between the original program and its mutants (i.e., kill the mutant). There are two different criteria for killing mutants: weakly killing mutants and strongly killing mutants, and this paper focuses on the latter. From our analysis, it is found that strongly killing mutants is essentially selecting the right paths in the control flow graph of the program. Based on this finding, two heuristics to strongly kill mutants are developed and an algorithm is provided to implement the heuristics.

articleTitle: On Safety Assurance of Symbolic Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has gained popularity in recent years. Symbolic Artificial Intelligence (symbolic AI), a subset of AI, holds significant promise, particularly in avionics software, offering potential enhancements to various aspects of its functionality, such as automatic decision inference or gen-erating optimal decisions. Despite its benefits, the integration of symbolic AI into avionics software introduces distinctive challenges, particularly in ensuring the safety and reliability of software powered by this technology. In this paper, we propose a set of supplementary objectives intended to support the DO-178C standard, specifically addressing features associated with symbolic AI. Additionally, we outline a set of metrics de-signed to support the generation of evidence for the proposed objectives. To illustrate the proposed assurance objectives, we made use of a TPN solution finder, which employs symbolic AI techniques to generate optimal routes for remotely piloted aircraft.

articleTitle: Different Control Methods for FES Cycling:Review
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Functional Electrical Stimulation (FES) is widely used in the rehabilitation of paralyzed patients. For patients with paralysis of the lower limbs, FES cycling is a practical way to help them in their rehabilitation. This paper mainly introduces the different control methods used in the process of FES cycling. They mainly cover PID control, adaptive control, fuzzy logic control, neural network control, and of course the combination of different control methods. The article summarizes the development progress of different types of control methods and compares the advantages and disadvantages of their application in FES cycling. Meanwhile, the future challenges and the work that needs to be accomplished are also prospected.

articleTitle: Leveraging Social Media Sentiments and Ethical Signals for NFT Valuation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: CryptoPunks has pioneered NFT innovations in digital art, spurring discussions on NFT valuation mechanics. While early research explored the societal and ethical impacts on CryptoPunks' price, the significance of post- 2021 social sentiment in NFT valuation remains unexplored. This paper analyzes how social media sentiments, coupled with factors like gender and skin tone, influence NFT valuations. Using data from social media, blockchain, and crypto exchanges, we demonstrate social sentiment's key role in CryptoPunks price prediction and highlight shifts in valuation mechanics post-2021. Our findings also indicate transaction and pricing imbalances based on gender and skin tone, even after controlling for NFT rarity and human-readable attributes. This research enriches studies bridging blockchain, ethics, and societal perspectives.

articleTitle: A Fine-Grained Emotion Prediction Method Based on Large Language Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Every day, much multimodal data emerges on social media. Previous studies have focused on the problem of fine-grained sentiment analysis in multimodal data. However, many multimodal data must be annotated for specific emotions to train fine-grained emotion prediction models. To efficiently train fine-grained emotion risk prediction models for multimodal data, we propose a few-shot learning-based method for multimodal fine-grained sentiment analysis. This model captures sentiment polarity in text using a pre-trained large language model, annotates a small amount of data, and generates a training dataset. Then, utilizing an intermediate layer fusion strategy, it combines representation vectors of text, images, videos, and audio to ultimately create a fine-grained emotion prediction model based on multimodal data. Exper-imental work on a real multimodal dataset, compared with random fine-grained sentiment analysis methods, shows that our proposed method has significant advantages in handling multimodal fine-grained sentiment analysis tasks and practical value.

articleTitle: A Creative Computing Approach to Forecasting Yield Shock of Winter Wheat
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: The United States stands as one of the world's largest wheat exporters, holding more than 10% of the global export market. Recognising the significant global economic repercussions that would arise from a negative yield shock of wheat, this study aims to use machine learning techniques to determine the key climate drivers of the winter wheat yield shock to facilitate forecasting three to six-month yield shock. Winter wheat is a strain of wheat that constitutes approximately 55% of total wheat plantations in the US. To accomplish this goal, this research uses a machine learning approach and employs support vector machines as a foundation. This research's findings reveal the designed model can achieve over 90% accuracy and ROC AUC score classification results. Notably, the temperature in the winter and spring months are identified, as well as the total precipitation of the autumn months would influence the forecast of yield shock the most. The result of this research validates the proposed approach that machine learning can be used to provide valuable information and thus can be applied when analysing other regions, e.g., the UK.

articleTitle: Test Adequacy Criteria for Metamorphic Testing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: The Oracle problem poses a fundamental challenge in software testing, seeking to validate the accuracy of a program's output given specific test inputs. Metamorphic testing (MT) has emerged as an automated technique to tackle the Oracle problem by testing programs against metamorphic relations (MRs) - crucial properties that persist across multiple executions of the target program. An essential aspect of software testing involves defining objective metrics to gauge the violation criteria. While many studies concentrate on the defect monitoring capability of MRs, the adequacy criteria for MT often lack coverage information regarding MRs. In this paper, we proposed MTcoverage, an adequacy criterion for MT. MTcoverage has integrated the degree of MR coverage into the adequacy criteria. We employed this criterion to formulate test case generation strategies. The effectiveness of this coverage criterion was also demonstrated by means of mutation testing. The results of this study contribute to enhancing the effectiveness of MT techniques for testing the program under examination.

articleTitle: Generating Adversarial Examples Using Parameter-Free Penalty Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Deep neural networks are extremely vulnerable to adversarial examples. An adversarial example is a perturbed input intended to cause deep neural networks to behave incorrectly. Despite much research about the techniques of generating adversarial perturbations, most optimization-based attacks that minimize the perturbations solve a constrained nonlinear programming problem by adding the misclassifying constraint to the objective function using a penalty parameter or a Lagrange multiplier, which is usually found by using binary search. However, this is inefficient due to the many iterations in binary search. The penalty method is one of the most commonly used iterative methods for solving constrained optimization prob-lems. It solves a constrained problem by converting it to an unconstrained one. In this work, we propose a novel white-box adversarial attack based on a parameter-free penalty method, which could generate adversarial examples with small perturbations at a high success rate. Extensive experiments on three test benches have been conducted, and results show that our method can obtain a good balance between the attack success rate and the perturbation size.

articleTitle: Search-Based Automated Program Repair: A Survey
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: This paper presents a review of state-of-the-art search-based automated program repair techniques, which are crucial for efficiently and accurately fixing bugs and vulnerabilities in software engineering. Traditional manual repair methods are increasingly seen as inadequate due to their high labor costs and time consumption. The versatility and applicability of search-based techniques have sparked significant interest in the software engineering community, driving a surge in research focused on developing more effective and efficient automated repair methods. The paper begins by introducing the foundational concepts and background of traditional automated program repair. It then delves into a detailed discussion of various search-based techniques and algorithms proposed in recent years. The review summarizes commonly used search-based frameworks, critically analyzing their strengths and limitations. It also provides a comparative analysis of different techniques concerning target languages, datasets, and other relevant aspects. In addition to evaluating current methodologies, the paper identifies ongoing challenges in the field and suggests potential directions for future research. By offering a thorough and systematic overview, this review aims to provide valuable insights and guidance for advancing the development and implementation of search-based automated program repair techniques.

articleTitle: Evolutionary Review of Research Themes in Functional Electrical Stimulation with in the Rehabilitation Medicine Field
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: The aging population and the increasing number of people are contributing to a rise in the incidence and mortality rates of diseases such as stroke and spinal cord injury, which present a significant threat to human survival. During rehabilitation, functional electrical stimulation (FES) has attracted significant attention as a medical intervention to enhance patients' rehabilitation outcomes and quality of life. Consequently, we employed the Dynamic Topic Modeling (DTM) approach to analyze and evaluate the topics, hotspots, and evolutionary pathways of relevant literature retrieved from the Web of Science between 2013 and 2023. The research findings indicate that within the field of rehabilitation, studies on functional electrical stimulation primarily focus on 8 themes, including rehabilitation technology and rehabilitation therapy. The research hotspots and pathways exhibit characteristics such as multi-technology combinations, interdisciplinary research, and personalized therapy, providing insights and guidance for future research on functional electrical stimulation in the field of rehabilitation.

articleTitle: Temporal Knowledge Graph Reasoning with Dual Guiding Constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Temporal knowledge graphs (TKGs) can store and model dynamic relational information. Recently, research on generative models has addressed the limitations of embedding methods in terms of generality and scalability. However, generative models still face two challenges in the context of TKGs: (1) Inability to effectively handle a large volume of contextual information;(2) Inability to constrain the rationality of generated results. To this end, we propose a new temporal graph reasoning framework, called the Dual Guiding constrained generative model (DuGen), which primarily consists of a context summarizer and a generative reasoner. The former generates crucial contextual information using question-guided prompts, while the latter employs a type decoder to infer the credibility of candidate entities. DuGen maintains the integrity and flexibility of individual model structures through external nesting. Experimental results demonstrate that DuGen outperforms state-of-the-art baseline techniques.

articleTitle: An Algorithm Based on Monocular Vision for Unsafe Behavior Recognition of Human-Object Interaction in Inspection Vehicles for Hazardous Chemical Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Autonomous inspection vehicles have been used as a potential technology for hazardous chemical storage safety monitoring research, but in this scenario, there are challenges such as strong interaction between human-object actions and difficulty in distinguishing similar actions based on monocular vision to identify unsafe behaviors. We propose an algorithm for identifying unsafe behavior in human-object interaction based on a multi-stream fusion network. Firstly, this algorithm classifies the initial action based on the PoseConv3D model in the human stream to improve its robustness against complex environmental interference. Next, the local features of the interacting objects are extracted based on the Yolo-SimAM model for the object stream. Finally, the human-object interaction stream discrimination module is designed to determine the relationship of keypoints between streams and derive the final behavior identification results. The experimental results show that our algorithm achieved better results in the self-built dataset of unsafe behavior in hazardous chemical storage.

articleTitle: DeepDTS: Diverse Test Selection Method for Deep Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) are extensively ap-plied in data-driven modeling tasks. Testing these networks is critical due to their involvement in safety-critical applications. However, their black-box nature poses challenges in explaining their decisions and identifying incorrect behaviors. Detecting faults in a DNN requires selecting a diverse and error-revealing test set from a vast, unlabeled dataset. Diversity in the test set expands the coverage of the decision space of DNN, aiding in the identification of distinct faults. In this paper, we introduce Singular Entropy Density (SED) metric to evaluate the diversity of a test set on a DNN model. We demonstrate its effectiveness against other diversity measures. Additionally, we present DeepDTS, a diverse test selection method designed to identify misclassified inputs with higher diversity scores according to SED. To evaluate the effectiveness of DeepDTS relative to other coverage and uncertainty-based test selection methods, we conducted experiments with widely employed datasets and DNN models. Our results demonstrate that Deep-DTS outperforms other selection methods in terms of selecting a diverse test set.

Index Terms: Output Of The Deep Neural Network

articleTitle: JFuzzer: Detecting Optimization Errors in JavaScript Just-In-Time Compilers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: As a crucial component of the internet, JavaScript plays an essential role in various web applications. However, to meet the demands of high-speed user experiences and an increasing array of functionalities, computationally intensive operations are becoming more frequent in JavaScript. This poses challenges for JavaScript engines. Consequently, in response to this situation, modern JavaScript engines are equipped with efficient just-in-time (JIT) compilers. Unfortu-nately, while optimizing code, JIT compiler introduces some security vulnerabilities due to its inherent complexity, thereby offering attackers a broad surface. In terms of vulnerability detection, fuzzing has consistently been considered an effective method for detecting bugs. However, existing JavaScript fuzzers are not mainly designed specifically for detecting JIT compiler vulnerabilities, making it challenging for them to uncover JIT-exclusive bugs. In this paper, we propose a new method called JFuzzer, specifically designed for detecting JIT compiler bugs. Specifically, we use some mutation strategies on the intermediate representation (IR) of JavaScript code to improve their syntactic and semantic correctness. On the other hand, we strive to ensure that the test cases can activate the JIT compiler each time. By employing the idea of differential testing, we compare the results when using the JavaScript engine's interpreter and the corresponding JIT compiler. This allows us to detect potential vulnerabilities in the JIT compiler. Through extensive experiments, our method has improved coverage on three widely used JavaScript engines.

articleTitle: Safety decision of autonomous driving behavior based on Bayesian network and its verification method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: With the increasing visibility of autonomous vehicles, the assurance of safe and precise behavioral decisions presents a substantial challenge within the realm of autonomous driving. The complexity of physical space, uncertainty in duration-space data, and human subjectivity complicate the assurance of existing behavior decision-making methods. To address these challenges, a safety decision method for autonomous driving based on Bayesian network is proposed. Firstly, semantic relations among risk elements in driving scenario are represented using knowledge graph, and the hierarchical structure and node information of the Bayesian network are determined based on expert knowledge and historical experience. Behavior decision actions are derived through Bayesian network inference. Secondly, leveraging the Bayesian network structure and inference results, a Duration-space Resource Timed Communicating Sequential Process is construct to verify the security of time and space resources. Thirdly, the constructed process is converted into Bigraphs and use the CPS MODEL CHECKER for security verification. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified using a highway lane change overtaking scenario.

articleTitle: An Ensemble Feature Selection Method Based on Symmetrical Uncertainty and Correlation for Software Defect Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Discovering and fixing potential defects in the software before it is put into use can ensure the reliability of the software. Software defect prediction technology enables the early detection and identification of software defects, thereby offering valuable insights for software testers to allocate their testing resources in a rational manner. This technology can enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of the testing process. However, the excessive dimension of features within software datasets poses a challenge, limiting both the efficiency and effectiveness of software defect prediction models. Thus, reducing the dimension of software datasets by eliminating irrelevant and redundant features that are not critical for defect prediction is of great significance in improving the performance of software defect prediction model. Comparative experiment has been implemented to evaluate and contrast the comprehensive application performance of seven classical feature selection algorithms when applied to diverse software datasets. This study introduces the principal component and proposes an improved algorithm C-SU (Correlation-Symmetric Uncertainty) based on Correlation Feature Selection and Symmetric Uncertainty. Due to its high stability, Random Forest is chosen as the classifier to establish the framework for the defect prediction model. To verify the validity of introduced method, it was in comparison to basic methods on datasets from eight open-source projects. The proposed feature selection method showcases superiority over other algorithms, as evidenced by the F1 score during model evaluation.

articleTitle: Centralization or Decentralization? How Can Digital Transformation Empowers Firm Performance?
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Digitalization is a systematic shift driven by information technology. It is a long-term strategy aimed at improving firms' economic performance and fostering sustainable development. In this study, we utilize big data from China's A-share listed enterprises spanning from 2007 to 2022 to empirically examine the mechanisms through which digitalization affects firm performance. Research indicates that firm digitalization has a positive impact on firm performance. Specifically, for every 1 unit increase in the degree of firm digitalization, its performance increases by 0.36% in the current year and 0.26% in the following year. The result remains robust after undergoing a series of robustness tests. Furthermore, ownership concentration exerts positive moderating effects. When the ownership concentration increases by 1 unit, the positive impact of digitalization on enterprise performance will increase by 0.0001 unit. This study provides practical recommendations for businesses to effectively utilize digital technologies and achieve high-quality development.

articleTitle: A Case Study into Collaborative Creation with Artificial Intelligence in Art Education in Taiwan
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: The exploration of Artificial Intelligence Generated Content (A.I.G.C.) in art education presents a transformative opportunity for multimedia programs, particularly within the Department of Comic Arts (D.C.A.), Tainan University of Technology, Taiwan. This paper delves into the dual studies conducted to assess the integration of A.I. art courses into academic curricula and develop cooperative production strategies using A.I.G.C. to enhance graphic computing. The primary objective of this research is to critically assess the benefits and impediments associated with the incorporation of A.I. art courses and to proffer strategic recommendations for their systemic integration into multimedia academic programs. The initial investigation aimed at integrating A.I.G.C. courses into the D.C.A. curriculum involved a series of AI-centric lectures and an extensive survey involving 92 students. The findings revealed a preference for elective A.I.G.C. courses, with most favoring lecture-based delivery over full curriculum integration. These results underscore the need for a balanced approach that respects traditional artistic values while embracing technological advancements. Furthermore, the second study focused on the “Summer Sunshine” project, employing Stable Diffusion and LoRA models to achieve high fidelity and consistency in manga production. This case study illustrated the practical efficiencies of A.I.G.C., from reducing manual labor to enhancing artistic quality, thereby setting new standards for A.I.'s role in graphic arts. Overall, the studies highlight the potential benefits and challenges of embedding A.I. art courses into curricula and demonstrate the effective use of A.I. in manga production through A.I.G.C. technologies. The findings from these investigations prompt broader discussions about the role of A.I. in art, advocating for policies that support ethical practices and nurture the coexistence of A.I. and traditional artistic methods.

articleTitle: Ada4DP: Adversarial Enhanced Dual-Attentive Aggregation Learning for Defect Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Software defect prediction (SDP) aims to assist practitioners for identifying defects quickly and efficiently, and to allocate limited software resources toward the most high-risk files to enhance software quality. Existing research mainly relies on manual feature engineering, metrics-based software quality assessment, machine learning for classifi-cation and identification, and other types. However, these methods are usually constrained, which can hinder the effectiveness of improving defect prediction. We propose a novel defect prediction method named Ada4DP, which combines deep semantic mining and data augmentation via adversarial learning. Ada4DP utilizes an encoder to extract semantic features from source code and employs adversarial learning (FGM) to perturb and augment the data, thereby mitigating the limitations of datasets. Moreover, we enhance the capture of source code context and explore additional semantics by integrating the Bi-GRU model with attention mechanisms. Additionally, Ada4DP can leverage the labels generated after prediction to enhance prediction accuracy through interactions between forward and backward classification by dual learning. Our experimental evaluation on 10 open-source projects from the PROMISE dataset demonstrates that Ada4DP is 11.6% higher than the baseline model in both within-project and cross-project defect prediction.

articleTitle: A Fault Analysis and Reasoning Method for Vehicle Information Systems Based on Knowledge Graphs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: In the information age, vehicle information systems are evolving with increased complexity. Traditional fault diagnosis methods struggle to keep pace with new software faults. Leveraging knowledge graphs, which can represent intricate connections and rules within language knowledge, offers a fresh approach. This paper introduces a comprehensive fault analysis and reasoning framework for vehicle information systems using knowledge graphs. By gathering internet data, conducting entity and relationship extraction, and constructing a knowledge graph, the model enables intelligent question-answering capabilities based on logical rule reasoning. Deep learning techniques, specifically the TransE model for knowledge representation learning, facilitate entity prediction, relationship prediction, and triple correctness verification. This framework aims to enhance fault diagnosis and maintenance guidance in vehicle information systems.

articleTitle: Methods for Removing Artifacts from EEG signals:A review
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Electroencephalogram signals are widely used in neuroscience and brain-computer interfaces. The EEG signals are relatively weak, so the devices for acquiring the EEG signals are very sensitive. Therefore, during EEG acquisition, interfering signals that are not EEG activity are usually mixed in, and these interferences are known as artifacts,and the most common of these artifacts are from physiological sources including electrooculographic (EOG) artifacts, electromyographic (EMG) artifacts, and electrocardiographic (ECG) artifacts. In order to know more accurately the intention of brain activity, after acquiring the EEG signal, some method must be taken to remove artifacts from it. The removal of these three artifacts is difficult and usually requires some specific methods to remove them. This paper describes the causes of these three artifacts and reviews the methods to eliminate them, and summarizes the advantages and disadvantages of these methods through the conclusions of the published literature.

articleTitle: The Impact of Digital Technology Application on Tourist Enterprise Performance: The Moderating Role of Ownership Balance Degree
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: The advancement of computer technology is progressing rapidly, and the digital economy is enabling the growth of micro-enterprises by enhancing quality. This study investigates how the application of digital technology can impact the performance of tourism enterprises within China's distinctive environment. In this study, the Python programming language is used to extract the annual reports of publicly traded tourism companies through machine learning techniques. Word frequency analysis is conducted on specific keywords related to the implementation of digital technology to evaluate the level of digital technology adoption within tourism enterprises. Subsequently, using data from Chinese A-share listed firms from 2007 to 2022, this paper reveals that the application of digital technology can have a positive impact on the performance of tourism enterprises. Within the mechanism, ownership balance has a positive moderating effect. Furthermore, the impact of digital technology application on the performance of tourism enterprises is more significant in Chinese non-high-tech and non-state-owned enterprises. To our knowledge, this paper is one of the pioneering studies that examines the relationship between digital technology application and tourism enterprise performance from the perspective of ownership structure.

articleTitle: Automatic Generation of Diagnostic Reports for Nasal Endoscopy Images: A Topic-Aware Multimodal Recurrent Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Background: To streamline physician workload, ensure coherence and interdependence among diagnostic descriptive sentences, and standardize reports, this study performs automatic assessment of nasal endoscopic images using deep learning techniques, and automatically generates diagnostic reports based on the assessment results. Methods: In our research, the dataset comprising nasal endoscopy images was constructed and divided into training, validation, and test subsets. The training set was further divided into samples ranging from easy to hard. We proposed a Topic-aware report generation model to achieve plausible, standardized, and homogenized diagnostic report generation. Results: Excellent performance was achieved by our model in diagnosing nasal diseases, with precision, recall, F 1 score, and accuracy scores of 94.91%, 85.17%, 89.77%, and 88.89%, respectively. High-quality diagnostic reports were generated, as indicated by BLEU, METEOR, and ROUGE-L scores of 0.3200, 0.2945, and 0.5210 respectively. Conclusions: Automatic generation of diagnostic reports in rhinoscopy using deep learning algorithms is feasible.

articleTitle: Construction of Urban Governance Portrait Based on Space-Air-Ground Integrated Digital Intelligence Pedestal
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: With the increasingly complex characteristics of cities, the development of urban governance is also hovering in the increasing uncertainty risk. In order to improve the level of urban governance and promote the development of smart cities, this paper, based on the existing research on urban portrait and urban governance, explores the methodology and architectural design of constructing an urban governance portrait based on an air-heaven-earth integrated digital intelligence pedestal from the perspective of digital intelligence-enabled social and economic development, and analyses its effectiveness through actual cases. The study has a novel perspective and practical depth, establishes a logical connection between urban portrait and urban governance, provides a clear idea for the construction and application of urban governance portrait, and broadens a new research horizon for data-enabled governance innovation, which will have a certain degree of popularity and exemplarity in the future.

articleTitle: Implications for Running AI Applications on Serverless Platforms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has garnered extensive attention due to its robust computational capabilities, efficient data handling, and superior accuracy. However, the complexity inherent in AI applications poses significant managerial and cost-related challenges for AI practitioners. There is a burgeoning trend towards leveraging serverless technologies to support AI applications, owing to their ease of deployment, automatic scalability, and cost-effectiveness. In this paper, we present a systematic performance evaluation of serverless applications with varying characteristics and structures on both X86 and ARM platforms. We utilize two of the most popular open-source serverless platforms, Knative and OpenFaaS, in our assessment. The insights gained from our evaluation are invaluable for the effective deployment of applications across X86 and ARM platforms. We are confident that the implications drawn from our experiments will not only inspire AI engineers to design more effective principles for AI applications on serverless platforms but also guide them in efficiently executing AI applications within such environments.

articleTitle: Evaluating Importance of Nodes in Interdependent Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Interdependent networks (INs) are typical Cyber-physical systems (CPS). INs are composed of two kinds of networks: the heterogeneous physical networks (PNs) and the heterogeneous communication networks (CNs), and they are interdependent together through power supply relation and information relation. However, INs are exposed to cross-domain cascading failures (CCFs) across CNs and PNs due to the interdependence. If we can identify and protect critical elements of INs, we can better prevent CCFs from the source with minimum cost. So, the accurate critical elements assessment of INs is of great importance for blocking the propagation of CCFs. In this paper, we solve the problem of evaluating importance of nodes in INs by the criteria of interdependent interconnected subnetwork (IIS). We use the importance of nodes to reasonably measure how influence of nodes removal on the connectivity of IIS in INs, as IIS guarantee the function of INs. The presented novel importance measure, shortest-path-function-loop-based node importance, can be useful in evaluating the importance of some percentage of nodes in INs. Some simulation experiments not only illustrate the effectiveness and accuracy of our measure compared with the widely used ones, but also highlight some non-supply nodes in PNs are more important than supply nodes.

articleTitle: Syntax-Dependency Orientation Guided Vision-and-Language Transformer for Image-Text Matching
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Image-text matching aims to bridge the semantic gap between visual and textual modalities, which is a fundamental task for multimodal learning applications. However, most Transformer-based multimodal retrieval model architectures ignore the capture and learning of textual semantic structures. To address this issue, we propose a novel architecture named Syntactic Dependency-Oriented Vision and Language Transformer (SDO-ViLT). Firstly, we introduce a syntax de-pendency parsing module that leverages directional syntax dependency graphs. Based on the syntax dependency graph with dependency directions, syntactic dependency features are obtained through Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs), enhancing the modeling capability of structural semantic relations. It enforces learning predicate-centric structured de-pendency semantics, thereby addressing ambiguity issues. Secondly, we propose a dependency distance-aware strategy. To address the limitations imposed by physical distance in text processing to expedite retrieval efficiency, we construct a dependency distance-aware attention mechanism that performs dependency tree pruning based on the dependency matrix. When computing the semantic matrix, we directly weight the core semantics represented by short dependency distances, enhancing the model's semantic understanding capability. The strategy retains the original accuracy while reducing the time required for text-image retrieval. A series of experiments are conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. The recall rate (R@ K) is improved on average by 1.7%, and up to 2.2% in the best case.

articleTitle: Experiment on the Effectiveness of Air-Space Numerical Intelligence Modeling for National Security Strategic Information Needs
