publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: With the increase of massive spatio-temporal big data of human mobility and the full spread of digital technology, the national security guarantee system with information security at its core is facing new challenges and impacts. Our aim is to explore how a widely available covariate describes the mobility management possibilities of information data so that its disordered mobility can be better modelled. Through validity experiments and spatio-temporal autocorrelation analyses of space-sky numerical intelligence modelling, we reveal the spatial patterns of monitoring the mobility of data-information populations. Our findings outline key correlates of mobility using widely available covariates, alleviating data bottlenecks in highly sensitive and sensitive datasets that are inaccessible to many researchers. In this paper, we present a novel methodology and framework based on spatial-numerical intelligence modelling to demonstrate how information flows of various information security concerns can be constructed for cross-cutting domains of research.

articleTitle: UrbanME: A New Benchmark for HD Map Elements Extraction in Urban Traffic Scenes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: High definition maps play a critical role in autonomous driving and navigation systems, providing vital driving information such as precise positioning and road details. Detecting and extracting map elements is a fundamental step in building accurate and comprehensive high precision maps. However, existing datasets primarily focus on semantic segmentation or object detection tasks and are not specifically designed to meet the needs of map construction. This paper introduces the Urban Map Elements dataset (UrbanME), a large scale 2D map elements dataset specifically curated for map construction purposes. The dataset consists of 16147 images collected from Chinese urban traffic environments, combined with 9998 images sourced from public datasets and annotated accordingly. It contains a total of 323,728 meticulously annotated instances of various high-quality map elements. We evaluate the performance of classical semantic segmentation methods using the UrbanME dataset as a baseline. The dataset includes multiple semantic categories and supports multiple annotation formats, providing a solid foundation for further research and advancements in map element extraction. Researchers can access the open source annotations of the UrbanME dataset at https://github.com/users/XueweiTang/projects/ for non-commercial scientific use.

articleTitle: Integrating Data-Driven and Knowledge-Driven Methodologies for Safety-Critical Scenario Generation in Autonomous Vehicle Validation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: Autonomous driving systems (ADS) enhance driving safety and efficiency but face significant challenges in safety-critical scenarios, necessitating thorough pre-deployment validation. Traditional knowledge-driven scenario generation methods are detailed yet slow and often insufficient for comprehensive ADS domain coverage. Conversely, data-driven approaches, employing real-world data and deep learning, offer efficiency but consume extensive computational resources and focus mainly on isolated domains. This paper introduces BridgeGen, a novel framework that integrates these methodologies to overcome their limitations. BridgeGen uses an ontology-based approach to convert abstract human knowledge into structured, symbol-based spatial constraints for efficient cross-domain exploration. Extensively tested with the Carla simulator, BridgeGen efficiently generates a diverse array of critical safety scenarios essential for robust ADS validation. Within this framework, we developed a scenario generation toolkit based on the ontology-based concept, assessing single-objective (PPO and PSO) and multi-objective (NSGA-II -DT) optimization algorithms. Our results indicate that PPO and PSO enhance critical scenario generation by 1.61 and 1.41 times, respectively, compared to baseline algorithms. NSGA-II -DT, used for multi-objective optimization, improves search quality and efficiency by 1.22 times, effectively avoiding local optima and ensuring broader scenario coverage.

articleTitle: LMSA:Lightweight Multi-Scale Attention Model for Garbage Detection Based on YOLOV5
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 24th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security Companion (QRS-C)
abstract: The challenges of small target detection, inference speed, and detection accuracy are key research areas in intelligent waste classification recognition, particularly the incorporation of attention mechanisms into algorithms. Existing self-attention mechanisms often face speed limitations due to low efficiency, particularly in MHSA's tensor reshaping and element-by-element computation, which are computationally intensive and challenging for embedded device deployment. To address these issues, this paper introduces a Lightweight Multi-Scale Attention Model (LMSA) based on YOLOV5 and the self-attention mechanism. The model constructs a new lightweight multi-scale attention module, utilizing a single memory-constrained MHSA between effective FFN layers to enhance channel communication while improving access efficiency. Additionally, a cascaded grouped attention module is proposed to provide different divisions of full features to the attention head, saving computational overhead and enhancing attention diversity. Experimental results demonstrate that on the VisDrone2021 dataset, the AP75 of LMSA is 41.43%, achieving the state-of-the-art (SOTA) among mainstream models. On a self-constructed dataset, the AP50 of LMSA reaches 74.55%. With equivalent accuracy, LMSA has lower computational power consumption, and the inference speed reaches 140fps on an RTX3090 graphics card. The model's advantages include fewer parameters, high accuracy, and fast inference speed, making it more suitable for embedded detection equipment and contributing to the intelligent development of waste detection.
